Iterates the active entity list, filtering for visible friendly units owned by another player, and draws an object marker for each (batching the locally-owned ones into a single combined count).
Walks the hit-ping list and unlinks/frees every entry whose expiry timestamp (offset 0xc) is at or before the current game time.

Walks the hit-ping list and unlinks/frees every entry whose first field matches the given key value.

Walks a linked list of string entries and draws each one as a vertically-stepped HUD text row with a one-pixel drop-shadow pass.
Writes the candidate unit pointer to the output parameter when it shares field 0xf0 with the reference unit, has type 0x19, and a nonzero value at offset 0xd4.

Probes the deploy site for nearby objects at two radii and writes a deploy-status code (0/1/2) plus a descriptive message string indicating whether a power cell will deploy as primary, backup, or be blocked.

Checks for a nearby power source within the required radius and whether its available power exceeds the item's draw, writing a deploy-status code and the corresponding will/will-not-deploy message string.
Dispatches deploy-status evaluation for the currently selected cargo type, handling enemy cargo, invalid types, power cells, and power-requiring items, and writes a status code plus message string.

Walks the basic-help line list freeing each node's text buffer, then clears the list container itself.

When the message ticker display is active, advances the ring-buffer index modulo its capacity and copies the next stored list entry into the display slot, returning that slot or null.
Returns floating-point 1.0 when the global byte flag at 0x00678c6a is non-zero and 0.0 otherwise, acting as a boolean predicate accessor.

Destructs a context-help entry by freeing its name string, walking and freeing its line list, and destroying the embedded list container.

Reads file lines (skipping a leading blank) into the entry's line list until the "{end}" marker, then matches the entry name against the context-help keyword table and stores the matched callback, returning true if a keyword matched.

Allocates and initializes a context-help entry with the duplicated name and two float fields, reads its text block, and either appends it to the global context-help list on a keyword match or destroys and frees it otherwise.
Opens the "help/context" file and, for each line parsed as a name and two floats via sscanf, creates a context-help entry from the following block of lines.
Walks the global message-log entry list, destroys and frees each entry's payload object, then resets the list head.

Walks the message-ticker entry list and, subject to several global gating flags, selects the entry whose elapsed/scalar timing value crosses its threshold, stamps it with the current time at offset 0x20, and returns a pointer to it.
Allocates and zero-initializes the two global message-log list containers (DAT_0067bd68/DAT_0067bd6c) under SEH and returns a pointer to them.
Frees every node string in both global message-log lists, then destroys and frees the two list containers themselves.

When the required game-state flags are all set, swaps the structure's two list-head pointers, frees the linked cargo chain hanging off the old list, clears the remaining list, and returns the resulting list pointer (or zero when the gating flags do not match).
Zero-initializes the two embedded list heads of the first message-log buffer pair (DAT_0067bd74/DAT_0067bd80) under SEH and returns the buffer base.
Frees all nodes of the two embedded lists in the first message-log buffer pair (DAT_0067bd80 then DAT_0067bd74) under SEH.
Zero-initializes the two embedded list heads of the second message-log buffer pair (DAT_0067bd8c/DAT_0067bd98) under SEH and returns the buffer base.
Frees all nodes of the two embedded lists in the second message-log buffer pair (DAT_0067bd98 then DAT_0067bd8c) under SEH.
Fetches the current message line string, computes its on-screen dwell time as length*0xAF clamped to a 3000-unit minimum, and starts the line's display timer.
Renders the message log then decrements the current line's display timer by the frame delta, advancing to the next line when it expires and returning true once the last line is reached.
Resets the global message-log line index/timer to the first line and starts that line's display timer using length*0xAF clamped to a 3000-unit minimum.
Allocates a 0x14-byte message-ticker display object, runs its constructor, and stores it in the global ticker pointer (or null on allocation failure).
Allocates a 12-byte message node, then walks the ticker queue by priority key and inserts the node at the correct sorted position.
Walks the message queue, resolves each entry's text via its virtual getter, and starts displaying the first non-empty message with a duration scaled to its length (minimum 3000).
When the game state permits HUD messages, fetches the next message if none is active, then draws/advances the current message and clears its slot when finished.
Word-wraps the input string to a column width derived from param_2/param_3, duplicating each resulting line and appending it to the output line list.

Returns true only when the game state flags indicate HUD ticker messages should be shown (in-game mode 3 with no blocking overlays active).

Scans the 3-int icon-slot array for the record whose id matches param_2 and resets that slot's fields to empty (-1/0).

Clamps the input distance to a maximum, scales it through configured factors and rounds to an integer interval, then clamps the result to a minimum of 400.

Tears down the squad info widget and markup document, then if confirmed sends a SQUAD_COMMAND packet carrying command code 2 (resign cancel).
Caches the current player name, frees any prior squadron markup documents, and rebuilds the squadron-disband panel with header labels, the charter pad, and a "DISBAND SQUAD!" button.

Closes the squadron-invitation dialog and, based on the button action (0=accept, 1=reject), either sends a join/decline request or shows a "CANNOT JOIN ANOTHER SQUAD"/"SQUAD JOIN REQUEST IN PROGRESS" message box.

Constructs the "OUTSTANDING INVITATIONS" window, building its column header, scrollable list view, and a "Reject All Invitations!" button, and stores the resulting widget in the global window pointer.
Clears the relevant pending-transaction flag and pops up the matching status message box for each squadron operation result code (establish/invite/oust/join/resign/disband success or failure).

Returns whether the local player may resign from their squadron, writing a "CANNOT RESIGN FROM SQUAD" title and a reason string (guest, not in a squad, is the owner, or data missing) into the output pointers.
Determines whether the local player may disband their squadron, rejecting guests, non-members, and non-owners, and returns an OK flag plus a title/body error message for display.
Handles the "Form A Squad" menu action: validates eligibility and on failure shows the error panel, then swaps the active selection widget to the form-squad target or the error panel.
Handles the "Invite Players" menu action: validates eligibility and on failure shows the error panel, then swaps the active selection widget to the invite-players target or the error panel.

Builds the squadron menu panel widget at the given rectangle, creates its six labeled action buttons (Invitations, Form, Invite, Oust, Resign, Disband), and lays them out vertically.
Attaches the squadron menu panel and every registered squadron button widget to the root UI container's child list.

Info_Widget virtual event handler that, for event type 1 whose subcode is in the range 5..7, tears down the widget via InfoWidget_Destroy and always returns true.

Constructs an Info_Widget bound to an explicit parent and existing child node, initializes its fields and vtable, and delegates to InfoWidget_Init for setup.

Looks up the "loading_screen" config texture and, if the renderer is ready, runs five present passes that clear the frame, blit the background image, draw the version banner, and flip the buffer.
Expands the stored axis min/max range to include the current raw reading and returns the normalized signed deflection (-1..+1) of that reading within the calibrated range.

Returns the current float value of a device-axis object (negated if its invert flag is set), or zero if joystick calibration is not yet active.
Allocates and constructs the three Joystick_Device_Axis objects (X, Y, throttle), binds each to its calibrated value global, and registers them with the input system.
Constructs a Joymap_Widget, zeroing its state fields, storing the parent pointer, installing its vtable, and setting its width/height from the global display-scale factor.
Marks calibration complete and commits the captured axis extremes as final calibration parameters, computing each center as the midpoint of its recorded min and max.
Advances the joystick calibration state machine at most every 500ms, transitioning through the center/circle/recenter/done/failed stages and rebuilding the calibration UI on each step.
Builds and returns the rich-text/HTML instruction string for the joystick calibration dialog corresponding to the current calibration state.
Rebuilds the joystick calibration map-frame UI by composing the rich-text instruction document, attaching the live joymap widget during active stages, and creating/laying out the calibration frame.
Draws the centered joystick-calibration quad for the given rect, then if both registered input axes are active draws the cursor reticle at the position given by their current axis values.

Lazily loads the calibration background texture and draws it, and if both input axes are working extends the recorded min/max calibration bounds from the current axis values, otherwise renders the "No working joystick detected." message.

Allocates and initializes the joystick-calibration UI screen, switches video mode if needed, loads the green-brown and blue background textures, wires the panel draw callbacks, and rebuilds the calibration UI.
Constructs the action-debug multigraph titled "Action [%d] (WHT raw)(YEL filter)(GRN sig)", adds a default timegraph, and configures its three plotted series and child-graph bounds.
If the action-debug multigraph exists, pushes the current scaled raw/filter/signal sample triple into the peek graph for this frame.
Lazily creates the action-debug multigraph and toggles it attached to or detached from the current target widget based on the active/visible state flags.

Stores a new target value and active flags on the action object, and if it differs from the table baseline and at least 100 ms have elapsed records the change timestamp and sets the global dirty flag.

Advances the action's smoothing filters for this frame, detects sign changes and threshold crossings of the filtered value, and on a confirmed transition latches the new value and raises the global action-changed flag.
Initializes the three smoothing-filter sub-objects of the action object (at +0x18, +0x48, +0x78) to zero and returns the object pointer.
Destroys the three smoothing-filter sub-objects of the action object (at +0x78, +0x48, +0x18) in reverse order.
Lazily allocates the global table of 22 state channels and resets each channel's fields, filters, sample lists, and current/target value caches to defaults.
Sets the target value for one channel and, if the channel is active, runs its update handler (type-5 vs default), caching the value when the handler declines to consume it.
Per-tick pass over all channels that ages each filter, recomputes the smoothed value, and emits a change event whenever a channel's value differs from its last broadcast value.
Allocates a channel-event record, fills it with the channel index and a remapped/ramped value, and appends it to the outbound event list.
Emits a channel-event for every channel index 1..21 using each channel's current cached value, forcing a full resync of the outbound event list.
Walks the subscription bucket for the current type and unlinks/frees every node whose type byte and id match the given key.
Replaces any existing subscription for the key, then allocates a type-0 (value) subscription node and inserts it into the table.
Replaces any existing subscription for the key, then allocates a type-1 (named/callback) subscription node, duplicating the supplied name string, and inserts it into the table.
Lazily creates the per-type subscription bucket list indexed by the node's type byte and appends the given subscription node to it.
Scans a subscription bucket for the entry whose capability mask is a subset of the query mask with the fewest extra bits, returning that best-matching subscription.
Walks a key binding list and strncmp-compares the given command name against each entry's name, returning 1 only if no entry matches (name not already bound).
Handles a key-down event by finding the best modifier-matching binding for the key code and either setting its pressed flag or invoking its press callback.
Handles a key-up event by iterating every binding in the key's list and clearing each pressed flag or invoking each release callback.
Routes an input event to the binding system, dispatching key-down for type 1 and key-up (by key code lookup in the keymap table) for type 2.
Compares two strings for case-insensitive equality, returning nonzero only when both reach their terminators together.
Scans the fixed command-descriptor table (0x58-byte stride) for an entry whose name matches the given string case-insensitively and returns its address.
Resolves a key name to its key-table entry, using a direct char-indexed lookup for single-character names and a case-insensitive named-key table search otherwise.
Matches a key-designation substring against the modifier-name table (e.g. Alt, Ctrl) and ORs the matched modifier's bit mask into the accumulated modifier flags.
Parses a key-designation string of dash-separated modifier tokens plus a key name into output key-entry and modifier-mask values.
Press/release callback for an axis binding that converts the button state into a 0.0/1.0 axis value and applies it (clamping a related slider when releasing).
Pushes a 0.0/1.0 press value for the key into the key-state dispatcher and, when the key (code 8) is pressed in a valid in-game context, fires gameplay event 14.
Walks the axis-binding list for bindings matching the given axis, applies each binding's response-curve function, and records the largest-magnitude positive and negative contributions.
For an enabled axis control, combines the positive/negative axis extremes (or default/return values) into a target and applies it to the bound slider via Slider_SetValueClamped.
Console command that parses a key designation, axis name, and relative/absolute mode, allocates and registers an axis-binding node, and replies "Okay." or an error string.
Console command that looks up the named input device and removes all of its registered bindings, replying with an error when the device is unknown.
Searches the registered-axis list for an entry whose name string-matches the query and returns that axis's associated value pointer, or 0 if none matches.

Initializes the input subsystem: allocates the key-binding hash table, fills the keycode-to-name table, registers commands and the named control axes (zoom_level, forward_thrust, etc.), and executes the keymap config file.
Finds the axis-binding node matching the given axis and key identifiers, unlinks it from the binding list, and returns the freed node (or 0 if not found).
Iterates every enabled axis binding, recomputes each bound control's value from its positive/negative axis extremes, clamps it to the control's min/max, and marks the control dirty.
Routes the argument to one of the handlers in the jump table, selecting the offline variant when the network/session global is null.
Computes and stores the clip-rectangle (origin, size, stride offset, right/bottom bounds) for the requested multi-pane split index into the active viewport descriptor.
Builds a viewport clip-rect descriptor from a top-left and bottom-right corner pair (selected by mode index), filling origin, width/height, stride offset, and inclusive right/bottom bounds.
If not already active, switches the current viewport to clip-mode 1 (full-screen) by loading its origin/size from the global full-screen rect and recomputing the stride offset and bounds.
If not already active, switches the current viewport to clip-mode 4 by hard-coding the fixed HUD 3D-view pane rect (origin 33,357, size 574x101) and recomputing its stride offset and bounds.
If not already active, switches the current viewport to clip-mode 2 by loading the main 3D scene pane rect from globals and recomputing its stride offset and bounds.

If not already active, switches to clip-mode 3 by building the scene rect (full or half-width depending on the renderer's split flag) and sets the dirty/refresh flag on each related framebuffer descriptor.
Records whether the high-resolution mode is active, then dispatches through a resolution-indexed handler table (640x480 vs other) to program the current viewport clip rect into the renderer.
Selects the 640x480 or high-resolution viewport handler from a function-pointer table based on the passed resolution flag and invokes it.

If the particle's expiry time has been reached, lazily creates its draw-list head node, allocates a 0x40-byte record from the arena, copies the 14-word particle payload into it, and links it onto the list.
Iterates the fixed-count particle array and then the linked overflow list, emitting every particle whose lifetime has expired into the draw list and returning the resulting list head.

Appends a transient light-flare record to the per-frame flare array, copying the source position from the given vec3, alpha and color parameters, and either a config-scaled RGB intensity or a default white tint.
Computes the integer bounding rectangle enclosing the persistent flare list and invalidates that region of the map texture via MapTexture_InvalidateRectRecursive.

Allocates a 0x38-byte persistent flare record for an entity, fills in its color, position from the entity transform, and back-pointer, links it into the persistent flare list, then invalidates the map bounds.
Writes the flare RGB color triple for an entity, choosing the friendly color when the entity team field matches the local player's team and the hostile color otherwise.
Unlinks and frees every persistent flare record whose back-pointer matches the given light entity (type 0x23), invalidating the map bounds after each removal.
Rebuilds the persistent flare list by first removing all existing flares for light entities (type 0x23) and then allocating a fresh team-colored flare record for each such entity in the world.
Transforms the vec3 in place by the 3x3 matrix supplied as nine consecutive elements, computing each output component as the dot of the original vector with a matrix row.
Builds a plane equation from three points, storing the normalized cross-product of the two edges as the normal and the negated dot of the normal with the first point as the plane distance.
Computes a polygon's face normal from its first three vertices via Plane_FromThreePoints and writes the normalized normal to the output vec3.
Computes the normalized vertex normal at the given vertex index of a polygon from the cross product of edges to its wrap-around neighboring vertices.
Returns true when the magnitude of the edge cross-product currently on the FPU stack is less than the given threshold, used to detect collinear/degenerate polygon vertices.
Walks the polygon's vertices, computes each vertex's edge normal, and removes any collinear vertex from both the position and UV lists, returning true if fewer than three vertices remain.

Constructs an edge-class (coplanar-polygon group) object from a seed polygon, initializing its member/leftover lists, copying the polygon plane equation and vertex count, registering it in the global edge-class list, and building its texture basis.
Iteratively grows an edge class by merging adjacent polygons that share an edge with its members, popping the work stack and selecting the resulting merged polygon for the class.
Cyclically rotates the polygon's vertex-position and UV lists by the given offset so a chosen vertex becomes the new starting vertex.

Removes collinear vertices, averages the per-vertex normals into a face normal, then finds the vertex whose local normal best aligns with the face normal and rotates the polygon so that vertex starts the list.
Destructor for an edge-class object that unregisters it from the global edge-class list and frees its member and leftover polygon lists.
Pops a seed polygon from the stack to create a new edge class, then distributes the remaining polygons into the class when they share an edge or onto its leftover list otherwise.
Computes the two texture-coordinate gradient (U and V) basis vectors for a polygon by solving the UV-versus-position deltas of its first three vertices in the face's local plane frame.
Stores a polygon's reference vertex position, reference UV, and computed U/V texture gradient vectors into the edge-class structure for later texture mapping.

Transforms each of the polygon's 3D vertices by the edge-class affine basis matrix (rows at this+0x40/0x50, origin at this+0x2c) and writes the resulting 2D coordinates into the polygon's parallel point list.

Scans the global edge-class list for an active class whose face normal is within the given angular tolerance of the polygon's normal and, if the polygon merges with one of that class's existing polygons, adds it to the class (otherwise returns true to signal a new class is needed).
Destroys a polygon vertex-dedup-map object by freeing each entry payload in its linked list at +4 and then tearing down its two member containers at +0xc and +0.
Builds a copy of the source polygon, remapping each vertex index through the shared dedup map (param_2) so duplicate vertices are unified, and copies the parallel 2D point list into the new polygon.
Computes the cross product of the two 2D edges formed by the polygon's first three points (points 0,1,2) and stores the signed Z component (twice the triangle area) into the output vector.

Searches the two polygons for a common edge (a vertex that appears in both with the next/previous neighbor matching in reverse winding), optionally requiring the two faces to be near-coplanar, and returns the two shared vertex indices via param_3/param_4.

Builds a new polygon that merges this polygon with param_1 along their shared edge (vertices param_2..param_3) by walking both vertex rings and copying the non-shared boundary vertices and their 2D points in order.

Computes the polygon's face normal by testing consecutive vertex triplets and returning the first edge cross product whose length exceeds the epsilon threshold (or a zero vector if every triplet is degenerate).

Tests whether the vertex at index unaff_EBX is convex by taking the cross product of its two adjacent edges and checking that its dot with the reference face normal is not on the wrong side of the negative tolerance.
Computes the polygon's face normal and returns true only if every vertex passes the per-vertex convexity test, i.e. the polygon is convex within the given tolerance.
If two polygons share a common edge segment, builds and returns their merged polygon (validating convexity), otherwise frees it and returns null.
Walks every polygon in the entity-class polygon list and returns true if any polygon references the given vertex index.
Removes and frees collinear/degenerate polygons from the first list and polygons whose vertices are no longer referenced from the second list.
Tries to merge the current polygon into an existing one; if that fails (or it is forced), allocates a new 0x60-byte polygon node, builds it, and flags it as shared when requested.
Drains the pending polygon queue, prunes degenerate/unused polys, then builds and returns a new hardened-geometry container with edge references reconciled against the merged polygons.
Allocates a mesh-hardening builder, feeds every polygon of the entity class through the insert-or-merge step, and returns the finalized hardened-geometry container.
Constructs a 0x18-byte mesh-hardening builder by initializing its two internal polygon lists.
Measures the length of the given login status message and stores its color byte and string pointer into the login-screen status-line globals.
Sets up the login "Choose a handle" prompt and creates a text-entry widget preloaded with the saved handle for the player to edit.
Sets up the login "Enter your password" prompt and creates a text-entry widget preloaded with the saved password for the player to edit.
Builds the "new handle / supply a password" login text-entry widget, seeds its edit buffer with the pending handle string from DAT_00679150, and registers it as the active login screen.
Dispatches on the server's Protocol::login_status code, switching the login UI to the appropriate prompt (new account, password, retry, etc.) or logging an unhandled-code error.
Allocates and initializes the login screen object (stored in DAT_005f35ec), wires up its vtable handlers, reads the saved WULFRAM registry handle index, and clears the login message-line globals.
Duplicates the entered account name and password into the login globals and, when the network channel is ready, builds and sends a LOGIN protocol message to the server.
Marks the login screen as active and, if both auto-login flags are set, clears the one-shot flag and immediately submits the stored credentials.
Draws a one-pixel-inset filled rectangle via the renderer's draw-quad and blit vtable entries (decompilation degraded; corners come in via registers).
Renders the login screen: draws the version banner and textured panels, then draws the login message lines plus optional Server/Account labels with their current values.
Tears down any prior dialog and builds the "ACCOUNT HANDLE REQUEST" InfoWidget with a Handle label, text-entry field, rich-text markup, and Okay/Exit Game buttons.
Removes each child id (listed at entry+0x10) from its hash bucket, bumps the global max-id watermark from entry+0xc, and unlinks the entry itself from the primary hash list.
Bumps the global max-id watermark from entry+0x10 and unlinks the entry from its secondary hash list.
Allocates and constructs the lost-OID hash bucket array of DAT_0067cd28 buckets (each 0xc bytes), or re-initializes the buckets in place if the array already exists.
Static initializer for the lost-OID subsystem: constructs the two node lists, sets the bucket count to 0x23, and builds the hash bucket table.
Static destructor for the lost-OID subsystem: destroys and frees the hash bucket array and tears down the two node lists.
Allocates an OID-set object {count, int* array} of the given size, aborting via lose_oid.cpp error and exit() if the requested size is negative.
Given an OID set, if its first OID is not already lost, allocates a delete_node, links it into the pending list, and marks every OID in the set into the hash table.
Searches the node list for an active hide_node matching the OID and, if none current covers the given threshold, allocates a new hide_node and links it into the pending list.
Returns whether the given OID is currently considered lost/hidden at the supplied threshold by checking the lost-OID hash table and the active hide_node list.
Constructs a Menu object, installing its vftable, default geometry/state fields, item-list, and the caller-supplied parent/position/style parameters.
Finds the message-list entry by id (or the current entry when id is -1), frees its old text, stores a strdup copy of the new string, and records the string length.
Allocates a new message-list entry holding a strdup'd text string, its length, the assigned id and two attribute fields, then inserts it into the message list.
Toggles the selectable/enabled flag (item+0x14) on the voice-data and related sound menu items according to the voice-capable feature flag DAT_006782ed and active player count.
Computes the column width, max item height and overall pixel bounds of a menu page, stores them in the menu struct, then clears the page surface and lays out each child item's sub-surface.
Re-lays out the menu, deselects the currently highlighted item via its vtable, resets the selected-item index to 0, and selects item 0 via its vtable.

Renders a menu page: clears the page surface, then for each item draws its background bar, optional selection highlight and label-arrow, and invokes the item's own draw vtable method at the computed position.
Closes the topmost open menu on the active menu stack, removing it from its parent surface and clearing its open flag, and returns true if a menu was popped.
Pushes the given menu onto the active menu stack, records its parent surface, marks menus active, and opens the menu by attaching it to the parent surface and setting its open flag.
Detaches and closes every open menu, empties the active menu stack, clears the menus-active flag, and marks all top-level windows as needing redraw.

Slider callback that computes the voice-playback volume ratio from the slider value, enables or disables the voice playback object accordingly, pushes the new gain into it, and refreshes the option label.

Slider callback that computes the voice-capture volume ratio from the slider value, toggles voice recording on or off, refreshes the option label, and pushes the new capture gain into the voice object.

Option-formatter callback that clamps the sound-mode index to 0-3, formats the matching label ("Use Hardware" / "Use Software [good/full HRTF]") into the shared option-text buffer, and returns the buffer pointer and clamped value.
Integer_Thermo callback that wraps the slider value to 0/1, formats the matching "Off"/"On" label into a static buffer, and returns the clamped index via the out-parameters.

Integer_Thermo callback that wraps the slider value to 0/1 and formats the matching label (donor-gated "Off - for donors only" / "On") into a static buffer, returning the clamped index via the out-parameters.
Thermo slider callback that converts the slider position into a gamma factor (2*pos / slider-max), pushes it to the render device via vtable slot 0x40, and stores it in the global gamma value.
Thermo slider callback that converts the slider position to a HUD/view-text size index (slider-max minus position) and applies it via the HUD layout updater.
Thermo slider callback that computes a view clip-plane scale (slider position / slider-max), stores it globally, and forwards it to Viewport_SetExtraClipPlaneScale.

When the render-device selection changed, duplicates the new device name and attempts to switch the active 3D device, committing on success or freeing the duplicate and restoring the previous device on failure.
Seeds the render-device Integer_Thermo with the current device index, invokes its format callback to produce the display label, and replaces the cached label string.
Seeds an Integer_Thermo with the current display-mode setting, invokes its format callback to produce the option label, and replaces the cached label string.

One-time builder that loads the menu bitmaps and constructs every options-menu widget (Thermo sliders, Word_Thermo toggles, Integer_Thermo selectors) for the sound, graphics, and gameplay settings pages, seeding each with its current config value.
If the effect manager exists, ticks all active emitters and, when the manager is enabled, spawns effect type 0x2d at the current ambient intensity.
If a sound device is active and ready, plays the menu selection/activation UI sound (id 0x19 or 0x2c depending on a flag) at the configured volume.
Activates the major mode: snapshots the current display config on first entry, runs the mode init/setup sequence, and stores the supplied flag byte.
When the mode is active, reloads player config and, if the display resolution/fullscreen settings changed, tears down and recreates the render device object and reapplies the windowed flag.
Renders one frame of the active major mode: integrates the menu sliders, invokes the current screen's draw method, and overlays the version banner.
Advances the menu's selected item index by the given delta with wraparound, firing the leave callback on the old item and the enter callback on the new item, then plays the selection sound.
Handles a UI input event by dispatching key-down codes to move the selection up/down, activate the current item, or back out of the mode, delegating unhandled events to the current selected item.
Destructor for a Major_Mode object: installs the Major_Mode vtable then runs the base-class destructor cleanup.
If a child screen is attached, draws the centered generic major-mode title string ("GENERIC 3MACS MAJOR MODE") via the renderer's text-draw vtable method.
Swaps the active child screen: detaches and notifies the previous screen, attaches the new one, and repositions/resizes it from its border and rect fields.
Allocates and initializes a 0x30-byte Major_Mode instance, setting default position/size fields, an empty selection index of -1, the Major_Mode vtable, and the "Generic Major Mode" name.

Skips leading whitespace then copies the next printable, non-whitespace token (up to 511 chars) from the input buffer into a local buffer, returns it as a strdup'd string, and reports the advanced cursor and remaining length via the output pointers.

Copies the tagmap rule's texture-id/mask arrays into temp buffers, sorts them via FUN_0049cc50, writes the sorted pairs back into the rule, and records the minimum texture priority byte and entry count into the rule header.
Scans the texture-id array for entries that duplicate the current id, OR-merges their bitmask into the kept entry, and compacts the array by swapping in the last element while shrinking the count.

Builds a tagmap substitution rule from up to four bitplane texture ids by deduplicating their masks, allocating a 0x1a-byte rule record, populating its texture-id/mask entries, and sorting it via TagMap_SortRuleEntries.

Parses a whitespace-separated tagmap rule line into up to four (texture-name, value) pairs, resolves each name to a texture index via FUN_004f5aa0, fills a 0x1a-byte rule record with the indices and XOR-masked values, and sorts it.
Reads the open tagmap2 file line by line and, for each line beginning with '+', parses it into a rule via TagMap_ParseRuleLine and appends the rule to the global tagmap rule list.
Builds the "maps/<mapName>/tagmap2" path, opens that file, and if present parses all its rules via TagMap_ParseRuleFile and closes it, returning whether the file was successfully opened.
Re-reads the map's tagmap2 file to build an old-to-new texture-index remap table from the rule list, then rewrites every tile texture reference in the global tile array through that table.
Composites a tagged texture by blending each source texture layer over the destination texture using its per-layer bitmask (dst = src&mask | dst&~mask) across the tile's pixel span.
Flattens the linked global tagmap rule list into a contiguous index array, frees the list, finalizes the rule set, and applies the texture remap to the loaded map via TagMap_RemapTileTextures.
Maps a scalar value through a color ramp, returning the clamped low/high endpoint color or the linked-list ramp entry at the normalized index.
Rebuilds the global elevation color ramp, filling its entry list with palette color bytes scaled per band and setting the ramp's min, max, and step from the world height bounds.
Rebuilds the global relief/shading color ramp, filling its entry list with scaled palette color bytes and setting its min, max, and step for the slope-shaded overview pass.
Renders the slope-shaded relief layer into the overview texture by sampling terrain gradient at each grid cell and writing the relief-ramp color byte.
Renders the base elevation layer into the overview texture by sampling terrain height at each grid cell and writing the elevation-ramp color byte.
Constructs a Medic_Client object, setting its vtable, looking up its type entry, and allocating and initializing the backing Medic_Vehicle instance.
Stores the given value into the Medic_Client object field at offset 0x14 (unidentified field; named by observable write).
Initializes the 256-entry shifted-character lookup table, mapping a-z to uppercase and the digit/punctuation keys to their shift-modified symbols.
Computes the length of the given C string and posts it as a console/chat message line via the message-queue append routine.
Posts a console message reporting whether a kudos request succeeded, or formats and posts a "Kudos request failed: %s" message on failure.
Lowercases the destination string and matches it against the message-destination name table, falling back to a player-name lookup, returning the resolved destination code or an error message.
Resolves the destination name and stores it as the active (and optionally default) chat message destination, or prints an error message if resolution fails.
Strips a leading slash, splits off the first whitespace-delimited destination token, sets it as the chat message destination, and returns a pointer to the remaining message text.
Compares two NUL-terminated strings two bytes at a time and returns true when they are exactly equal.
Skips leading spaces, NUL-terminates the next space-delimited word in place, and advances the caller's pointer past it.
Builds and prints the contents of the text or voice ignore list (selected by the flag), or a message saying the list is empty.
Resolves a player name, locates the player in the roster, adds them to the text or voice ignore list, and prints the result message.
Removes the named player from the text or voice ignore list and prints the result, or prints the current ignore list when no name is given.
Handles the "/filter {on|off}" command by toggling the profanity-filter flag, reloading the player config and filter file, and printing the filter status or usage text.
Returns true only if the string contains none of the special characters < > ^ & backslash slash or double-quote.
Parses a kudos/ding/endorse chat command, validates the target player name and point amount, then builds and sends a points-transfer message or reports a usage/validation error.
Tokenizes a slash-command string and dispatches it to the matching handler (ignore, ignorevoice, noignore, filter, kudos, ding, endorse) or reports an unknown-command error.
Inspects the first character of a typed chat line and routes it to the slash-command dispatcher, the '/' handler, or sends it as a normal channel message depending on the current channel mode.
Copies the current chat input-buffer text, routes it for processing, sends a COMM_MESSAGE_REQUEST packet with the channel and recipient, clears the input field, and frees the temporary copy.
Returns the destination label string ("SERVER", "TARGET", a player name, etc.) for the current chat channel mode selected in DAT_005f36b8.
Handles a key event for the active chat input field: escape (0xd) cancels and clears the field, enter (0xc) submits the line, otherwise the event is forwarded to the underlying text-edit widget.

When the chat input field is active, consumes printable and control key events (0xc/0xd/0xe/0x91) by routing them to the key handler and returns true, otherwise returns false to let the event pass through.
Initializes the chat subsystem: allocates and constructs the chat-controller object into DAT_00678428 and sets the default channel mode (3) and recipient.
Formats the "Message (to %s):" chat prompt into the global buffer and outputs its address, length, and the current input-buffer pointer and length through the caller-supplied output pointers.
Initializes the global table of network bandwidth/rate threshold and step values (0x15, 0x55, 0x155, ... 0x15555) and then calls the dependent setup routine.
Iterates the active index buffer backward, scaling each triangle's vertex coordinates by the mip-level scale factor and dithering each into the indexed (paletted) downsample target.
Iterates the active index buffer backward, scaling each triangle's vertex coordinates by the mip-level scale factor and pseudo-bilinearly downsampling its rows into the destination image.
Lazily loads the "brown/20" border texture, blits four tiled border strips around the screen edges, then draws the inner and outer rectangle outlines that frame the HUD viewport.
When the controls-help panel is dirty, frees its current markup document, invokes the widget's reset callback, creates a fresh rich-text document, and clears the dirty flag.
Lazily allocates and constructs the controls-help panel widget if it does not yet exist, positions it within the screen bounds, and caches the current font reference into it.

Builds the controls-help screen by allocating its callback object and main UI container, wiring their vtables and handler pointers, switching screen mode if needed, and ensuring the help panel exists.
Compares the requested source string to the current help-document source and, if different, marks the panel dirty, frees the old string, and stores a strdup copy of the new one.

Reads the axis's raw target value, stores it as the previous sample, and advances the smoothed axis position by the per-frame delta scaled by the configured smoothing factor (or 1.0 when smoothing is disabled).
Zeroes the accumulated value and sets the reset flag on each of the three mouse device axes (X, Y, Z).
Constructs the three Mouse_Device_Axis objects named "mousex", "mousey", and "mousez" and registers each with the input device-axis system.
Snapshots an entity's physics state (control-block link, position, velocity, orientation, and matrix rows) into the given save buffer prior to a prediction step.
Restores an entity's previously-saved physics state (control-block link, position, velocity, orientation, and matrix rows) from the save buffer and re-derives dependent matrices.
Returns true when a contact record's two flags and (when set) its two position vectors exactly match the saved prediction state block, used to confirm a predicted collision still holds.
Captures the local player's predicted collision result (flags, position, orientation, and a 24-word matrix block) into the global prediction-state buffer at DAT_0067cde8.
Writes a new XYZ position into the entity and re-derives its dependent transform/bounds via the two matrix-rebuild helpers.

When a fresh prediction is pending, saves the local player's physics state, applies the predicted position/orientation, re-simulates movement, and on success commits it (otherwise rolls the state back).

Collision callback that, when a contact involves the local player and matches the saved prediction state, accumulates hit statistics and records a fresh predicted-contact result for replay next frame.

Fires the entity's slot-0 weapon when its recharge timer expires, resolving the muzzle transform and target, queuing the firing transient FX, and emitting a hit event if a valid non-friendly target was found.

Walks every active entity and decrements each of its 13 component recharge timers by the frame delta, firing the slot-0 and slot-11 expiry handlers and reloading the timer to its component's recharge period when a timer reaches zero.
Splits the elapsed tick time (capped at 0x226) into up to five substeps and advances the world simulation by each substep, rendering/syncing the active scene object on each pass.

Per-frame entity interpolation tick: walks the active interp-record list, advances each entity toward its target via Interp_StepEntity, frees stale records, samples the local player's altitude to the peek graph, and runs the smoothing/finalization passes.
Exponential low-pass filter that updates the running average and deviation of a timing/latency sample, snapping to the raw value on a reset flag or when the active-network state toggles.
Stores the three components of an interpolation offset/position vector into globals and records each component as a peek-graph sample stamped with the current time.
Computes the delta between the current time and a packet timestamp, feeds it to the latency smoothing filter, and (when networked) records the bias-corrected offset via Interp_RecordPositionSamples.

Compares the entity's current and target orientation quaternions and, once their dot products both exceed the convergence threshold, clears the active orientation-interpolation flags and sets the converged-this-frame global.
Advances the orientation-error accumulator by the frame step and stores the smaller of the two current/target quaternion dot products as this frame's orientation error metric.
Records the scaled accumulated orientation-error metric as a peek-graph sample stamped with the current time, then resets the accumulator to zero.

Advances one entity's dead-reckoned state for the elapsed time: lazily allocates its interp record, extrapolates position and orientation toward the network target, and for the local player accumulates the error metrics and mirrors the result into the prediction globals, returning whether the record is still active.
Walks the interp-record list and removes/frees every record whose owner id matches the given entity id.
Allocates and constructs the entity-interpolation manager singletons (a control object plus a 0x16-element array of interp slots) and stores them in the global pointers.
Clears all queued lag events, then frees the per-id float accumulator struct and the per-id list-head array themselves.
Zeroes the per-id float accumulator struct and frees every queued event node across all 21 per-id lag-event lists.
Walks one event list, adds the given time offset to each event's release-time field, and re-inserts each event into its target per-id lag list.
Iterates all 21 per-id lag lists, dequeues events whose release time has arrived, and integrates the weighted elapsed time into each id's float accumulators.
Optionally reschedules pending lag events, then frees every node of the outgoing action-update queue and clears its head pointer.
Allocates and constructs the local player's vehicle client object as a Tank or Medic depending on the session vehicle class id, storing it in the global player pointer.
Builds a transient impact/hit effect event from the local player's current state and queues a copy of it for rendering.

Per-tick local-player vehicle update that decrements the shake timer, runs bandwidth/connection and terrain-proximity checks, and links the entity into the active render list, returning whether it was added.
Tears down all client world state: clears the lag queues, frees entity lists and per-entity buffers, resets HUD/state flags, and destroys the local player vehicle object.
Resets the local player's effect timer to now+1000ms and triggers a 1000ms camera/screen shake on the active view.
Builds a unique client identifier string from the host name, current process ID, and UTC timestamp ("[host-pid-YYYY:jjj:HH:MM:SS]") and returns a strdup'd copy.
Ensures the global client name is at least 15 characters long, falling back to a generated client ID, and if it changed replaces the stored name and reloads the player config.
Allocates and constructs the global socket-manager and packet-dispatcher objects under SEH and configures the manager's worker thread count.

Opens a TCP connection to the given server host (defaulting to localhost), attaches the packet handler, sets connection timeout/keepalive parameters, marks the connection active, and updates the client name.
Opens the UDP connection on the given port, binds the packet handler, and sends the initial "Hello There" and HELLO handshake packets to the server.
Sends a HELLO handshake packet (subtype 1) carrying the local player name string to the server.
Sends the final HELLO handshake packet (subtype 2) over the TCP connection, marks the session as joined, and triggers post-connect setup.
Sends a final "Hello There" packet, closes the UDP connection, and records the disconnect timestamp.
Clears the connected flag, shuts down and destroys the active connection and socket manager, runs cleanup callbacks, and exits the app if flagged to do so.
Pumps the connection inside a setjmp error guard: drains pending received packets, dispatches them, and tears the connection down when the link reports it has closed.
Tears down the active network session: flushes pending packets, kills any in-progress connection, runs disconnect callbacks, and zeroes the session/client state globals.
Marks the connection as established once data has arrived, otherwise after a 20-second timeout shows the fatal network message and switches to the error screen.
Builds and sends a BEACON_MODIFY (opcode 0x3b) network message carrying the given beacon id plus a zeroed position vector.
Builds and sends a BPS_REQUEST (opcode 0x4e) network message carrying the given integer argument.
Forwards an incoming chat/text message to the chat handler unless it is a filtered channel type or an echo of the local player's own message.
Creates a LOGIN (opcode 0x21) network message and submits the username and password credentials for it.
Builds and sends a REINCARNATE (opcode 0x25) spawn message with the requested vehicle type, current base id, and two computed spawn parameters, then sets the respawn-pending flag.
Builds and sends a REINCARNATE (opcode 0x25) selection message in sub-mode 1 carrying the chosen item/slot byte.
Builds and sends a RETARGET (opcode 0x26) network message carrying the current weapon/target mode flag and the given target id.
Once the scheduled next-ping time is reached, builds and sends an opcode-8 keepalive message with the payload string "ping".
Builds a ROUTING_PING network message (opcode 0x4c), appends the two byte arguments, and queues it on the active connection.
Adds the current frame time to the outbound-rate running average, sends a movement update packet while the rate counter is below 5, then finalizes the average for this frame.

Once at least 200ms have elapsed since the last send, builds an INPUT_FEEDBACK message (opcode 0x40) carrying the accumulated input counter, resets that counter, and queues it on the active connection.
Builds a SQUAD_CREATE network message (opcode 0x42) containing the local player id and four squad name/tag strings, and queues it on the active connection.
Builds a SQUAD_INVITE network message (opcode 0x46) containing four string arguments and queues it on the active connection.
Serializes the given kudos record into a KUDOS network message (opcode 0x4f) and queues it on the active connection.
When voice chat is enabled, builds a GENERIC message (opcode 0x54) with key "want_voice_data" and the given on/off flag, and queues it on the active connection.
Detects a change in the voice volume/level global and, when it changes, sends a want_voice_data on/off request reflecting whether the level is positive.
Initializes the network message dispatcher by registering each opcode's handler callback, channel/priority class, and group labels for the protocol's incoming message types.
Finds or lazily creates the per-id handler entry in the global list (capacity 6) keyed by the current id and dispatches the given message payload to it.
Walks the pending-ACK linked list, frees each node's payload buffer and returns every node to the ACK node pool, emptying the list.
Counts how many leading pending-ACK entries fit within the ~400-byte packet size budget, capping the result at 200.
Builds and sends an "ACK1" network packet containing the fitting pending-ACK entries and their item ids, dequeuing and freeing each entry as it is written.
Throttled by elapsed time (or forced by the flag), sends an "ACTION_DUMP" packet containing the full set of action/control axis values for the given entity.
Sends an "ACTION_UPDATE" packet carrying only the changed action axis values from the supplied dirty-list for the current entity.
When connection state permits and the ping interval has elapsed, sends a "PING_REQUEST" packet carrying the given timestamp/id.
When connection state permits and the ping interval has elapsed, sends a "PING" packet echoing the given timestamp/id back to the peer.
Decodes a received "TRANSIENT_ARRAY" packet, reading each transient FX record (type, position, optional target) and queuing or dispatching the corresponding effect event.
Handles a received "UPDATE_ARRAY" packet by delegating to the entity-update array decoder and then closing the message reader.
Decodes a received "LAG_FIX" packet, reading the lag-compensation tick value and an accompanying flag byte.
Builds an outgoing network message by writing a type byte plus two strings, and for types 2-4 also writes a freed array of extra strings followed by a trailing global string, then dispatches it.
Parses an incoming WORLD_STATS packet, resets the game session and applies the new world parameters, then sends a WANT_UPDATES acknowledgement reply.
Parses an incoming HELLO handshake packet and, depending on its subtype byte, validates the protocol version, sets the local player id, stores a received buffer, or triggers the post-handshake step.
Parses an incoming PLAYER packet to set the local player id and a flag, then kicks off a bandwidth request and ensures the voice channel is connected.

Parses an incoming tank/unit spawn packet and creates the object with its position and orientation, falling back to a TANK_RESEND_REQUEST reply if creation fails or entering the world if the object already exists.

Parses an incoming DELETE_OBJECT packet, looks up each listed object and spawns its death/removal effects before destroying it, recording the deleted object ids into a lose-oid set for acknowledgement.
Parses an incoming ADD_TO_ROSTER packet describing a player (id, team, colors, name, score) and adds that entry to the scoreboard roster.
Parses an incoming UPDATE_STATS packet and updates an existing roster player's team, colors, score and other scoreboard statistics.
Parses an incoming BIRTH_NOTICE packet, finds the matching roster player node by id, and marks it as born/alive while storing the supplied value.
Looks up a named string value and, if found, builds and dispatches a STRING_VALUE network message carrying its key and string payload.
Builds and sends a BEACON_REQUEST (opcode 0x3a) packet carrying the entity id and a position vector with the default "new"/"No comment." labels.
Builds and sends a BEACON_MODIFY (opcode 0x3b) packet with the beacon entity id, an enable/visible flag, a position vector, and the (NULL-coalesced) label and comment strings.
Parses an incoming COMM_MESSAGE packet (sender/target ids and channels plus a text string) and dispatches it to the chat/comm display handler before freeing the string.
Parses an incoming LOGIN_STATUS packet, forwards the status code to the login handler, and on status 8 records the admin/privileged flag into the global login state.
Parses an incoming BEHAVIOR packet, deserializing the full set of server-driven gameplay tuning globals (flags, float/int rates, and physics parameters) into their global variables.
Parses an incoming SHIP_STATUS packet (entity id, type/flags, and name) and adds or updates the corresponding map marker label.
Parses an incoming TEAM_INFO packet, building two heap team-descriptor structs (side 1 and side 2) from a flag byte plus five duplicated name strings each, then installs them via Team_InitSides.
Parses an incoming CARRYING_INFO packet (entity id and several status bytes) and updates the carried-cargo state for the indicated item.
Parses an incoming UPLINK_INFO packet (team-slot index plus two status values) and updates the corresponding team slot's status.
Parses an incoming REINCARNATE packet, maps the respawn reason code to a sound/event index, optionally plays the death-pitch-adjusted audio cue, and resets the local respawn state globals.

Parses a GAME_CLOCK network packet, starts or stops the clock's continuous tick sound depending on the running/paused flag, and updates the global game-clock state, timer object, and elapsed-time globals.
Parses a WARP_STATUS network packet and walks the full map cell grid, reading one status-flag byte per cell and applying it to update each map cell's warp/scan state.
Parses a CONTINUOUS_SOUND network packet and, when connected to a valid player object, stops the active continuous sound emitter identified by the given sound id.

Reads one translation-ramp record from the packet stream (mode, frame count, two scanf-parsed float bounds) and configures the target ramp entry's mode bitmask and value range with precomputed reciprocals.
Handles a TRANSLATION network packet by reallocating and initializing the 0x700-byte global translation-ramp table, parsing all ramp entries into it, and queuing the corresponding client event.
Zero-initializes every ramp entry of a freshly allocated translation table (16 entries from the base plus 12 more starting at offset 0x400) and returns the table base.
Parses a STRING_VALUE network packet (type id plus a length-prefixed string) and dispatches the string to the registered client-event callback for that type.
Parses a VERSION_ERROR network packet, stores the server's required/reported version numbers into globals, and raises the version-mismatch flag.
Parses a RESET_GAME network packet and clears all map cell state, freeing per-cell scan objects across the entire grid.
Parses a SHUTDOWN network packet (flag plus optional message string) and triggers the client disconnect/shutdown handler, switching screen mode and storing the shutdown message.
Parses a SQUAD_RESULT packet (u16 result code plus a heap-allocated message string) and displays the squad transaction outcome via SquadUI_ShowTransactionResult.
Parses a ROUTING_PING packet (u32 source index plus a byte destination index) and records the current ping/round-trip time into the routing latency table for that source/destination pair.
Handles an IDENTIFIED_UDP packet by clearing the pending-UDP-identification flag and switching the screen to mode 0xB.

Parses a BPS_RREQUEST reply (u32 bandwidth value plus a granted flag); on grant it stores the new bandwidth cap and reloads the player config, otherwise it restores the prior cap and shows a Restricted Bandwidth dialog.
Parses a SQUAD_DEFINITION member record into a newly allocated 0x28-byte entry and inserts or replaces it in the squad member list, then refreshes the squad roster UI.
Parses a SQUAD_DEFINITION record into a newly allocated 0x24-byte entry and inserts or replaces it in the squad definition list keyed by id.
Parses a SQUAD_DEFINITION invite record into a newly allocated 0x2C-byte entry and adds it to the squad-invite list, printing a "has invited you to join" console notice.
Parses a KUDOS packet and, by record type, either reports a kudos request result to the UI (type 2) or stores the received kudos count global (type 3).
Handles a MILTAB packet by reading the military/leaderboard table rows from the packet stream into the global MilTab array.
Parses a VIDEOMSG packet (two heap strings plus an acknowledged flag) and dispatches the ban/warn/announcement video message handler, freeing the temporary strings afterward.
Lazily allocates and constructs the global timed entity-hold list singleton on first use and returns a pointer to the global handle.
Walks the timed entity-hold list freeing each record and its saved-state buffer, frees the list itself, and clears the global handle.

Adds or refreshes a hold record for the given entity, snapshotting the entity+0xC0 link into a freshly allocated 6-byte buffer, redirecting that link to the buffer, and (re)arming a 3000-unit expiry timer.
Decrements every hold record's timer by the per-frame delta and, for any that expire, restores the entity+0xC0 link from the saved pointer before unlinking and freeing the record and its buffer.
Finds the hold record for the given entity pointer and, if present, unlinks it from the list and frees the record and its saved-state buffer.
Resets the outbound bandwidth/send-rate throttle state to defaults, setting the mode to 4, seeding the rate from the configured default, and zeroing all counters and flags.
Tests a proposed packet byte count against the current bandwidth budget, updating the send-tick marker and the over-budget flag, and returns whether the send is permitted this tick.
Caches the current process and thread handles and stores duplicated copies of the machine and user names (with fallback strings) into globals.
Tokenizes GetCommandLineA into whitespace- and quote-delimited arguments, then stores the argument count and a newly allocated argv pointer array into the global command-line state.

Client startup sequence that loads the lock-screen video, wires up the global callback table, initializes subsystems and team status slots, parses client_params, brings up the Glide renderer, and enters Client_Main.
Stores a flag byte into a global and writes it to offset +8 of the two named registered input-device axes (e.g. invert/enable state).
Runs the SlurpySoft CSNUI auto-updater, skipping when a "do_not_update" marker exists and otherwise checking www.wulfram.com for the wulfram2_client or betawulf channel.
atexit handler that releases/cleans up the "videos/lock.xml" resource on shutdown.
Stores the application HINSTANCE in a global, registers the lock-video atexit cleanup, and runs the early startup init routines.
Formats a printf-style message with wvsprintfA into a 2000-byte buffer and writes it to the open crash-report file handle via WriteFile.
Converts a FILETIME to local time and formats it as a "M/D/YYYY HH:MM:SS" string, writing an empty string on failure.
For a loaded module base, validates the MZ/PE headers and logs its filename, load address, file size, PE timestamp, and on-disk file date to the crash report.
Walks the process virtual address space with VirtualQuery and logs every committed module's info to the crash report via CrashLog_DumpModuleInfo.
Writes the crash-report header recording the current time, executable path, user name, processor count/type, and physical memory size.
Multiplies twelve double-precision transform fields of the object by a global scalar factor (scaling its position/orientation components).
Computes the mip level (0-8) for a textured polygon from its screen-space UV gradient area scaled by the texture's LOD bias, by repeatedly multiplying a ratio threshold until it exceeds the coverage.
Initializes the software rasterizer global state by copying configuration constants, building a 1.0/n reciprocal table for n=1..16, and filling a 256-entry table with 0xff.
Loads per-mip-level rasterizer globals (texture base, stride, shift counts and U/V wrap masks) from indexed lookup tables for the selected mip level.
Sorts the three triangle vertices by screen Y, builds the long and two short edge span interpolators, and rasterizes the upper and lower halves by calling the selected span-fill routine.

Chooses the LOD region from the polygon's three vertex coordinates, builds the texture-projection matrix, selects the mip level, clamps it, and loads the per-mip rasterizer state for the upcoming triangle.
Triangulates a vertex/UV polygon as a fan, setting up texture state and rasterizing each triangle while incrementing the rendered-primitive counter.

Walks a buffer of 0x54-byte render primitives back-to-front, either invoking each entry's callback or copying its vertices/UVs and setting up and drawing a textured triangle, then adds the batch count to the primitive counter.
Advances a triangle edge's span interpolator by one scanline, accumulating the fixed-point X and texture-coordinate error terms and applying the extra step on overflow/carry.
Computes the vertical scanline range and per-scanline X step/error deltas for one triangle edge between two vertices, writing the results into the edge interpolator struct.

Computes a triangle edge's scanline range and X deltas like Rast_SetupEdgeSpan and additionally derives the per-vertex texture/perspective gradient terms from the view matrix into the edge interpolator struct.
Rasterizes each queued scanline span as an opaque perspective-correct textured run, dividing by the interpolated 1/z every 16 pixels and copying texels from the active texture into the framebuffer.
Looks up a palette shade/translucency remap table for the given color and recolors every pixel of each queued scanline span by indexing the existing framebuffer value through that table.

Rasterizes each queued scanline span as a color-keyed perspective-correct textured run, dividing by the interpolated 1/z every 16 pixels and writing only non-zero texels so index-0 pixels stay transparent.

Rasterizes each queued scanline span as an opaque affine (linearly interpolated, non-perspective) textured run, stepping fixed-point U/V across the span and copying texels from the active texture into the framebuffer.

Allocates and populates the span-rasterizer dispatch tables, filling each draw-mode slot with the affine, perspective-opaque, fill, perspective-masked, or palette-remap span routine and mirroring the table into the secondary and static copies.
Fills the DAT_005f3d30 lookup table so that each span-length bucket up to 2^bit maps to a decreasing mip/shift level from 8 down to 0.
Converts the two floating-point U/V coordinates to fixed point, masks them to the texture dimensions, and returns the single texel sampled from the indexed surface using its row stride.
Constructs a Piecewise_Viewer instance, installing its vftable, zeroing its state fields, storing the supplied curve pointer, and initializing its two embedded sub-objects.
Destroys a Piecewise_Viewer instance, restoring its vftable, tearing down its two embedded sub-objects, and invoking the base-class destructor.

Renders the piecewise-curve editor widget: draws its background and frame, the value/time grid lines and axis labels, the plotted curve points and transient markers from two linked lists (decrementing each entry's lifetime and freeing expired ones), and handles click-to-edit hit testing against the curve.
Dispatches a key/command event to the network-performance overlay, toggling display flags and adjusting the graph scale or invoking the bound callbacks based on the key code.
Reads the network clock's current time in seconds, scales it to milliseconds, rounds to an integer, and wraps negative results back into range.

Computes the round-trip delay from the send/receive timestamps and folds it into the smoothed RTT estimate using an averaging weight that depends on sample count and whether the new delay exceeds the current estimate.
Records the current frame's last round-trip delta into the network performance graph keyed by the scaled current game time.
Computes an expected reply time (a fixed offset, or one derived from the tick rate when in live online play) and stores it into the network clock's pending-ping deadline field.
Advances the network clock for this frame, records the RTT graph sample, and when a ping is due sends either a plain ping or a timestamped ping request and primes the next ping deadline.
Validates an incoming ping reply against the outstanding request window, and if its round-trip is within tolerance feeds the latency back into the network clock and records it on the latency graph.

Blends the network clock's current time with the smoothed RTT estimate using a queue-depth weighted factor, clamps it to be no earlier than the raw clock, and returns the result rounded to milliseconds.

Processes a server time update by refreshing the RTT estimate, validating the reply, recomputing the smoothed and tick-aligned client times, recording the per-channel clock offset, and logging it to the latency graph.
Resets the network clock smoothing state and allocates or re-initializes the global clock object under SEH protection.
Walks the cached player-stats record list comparing each entry's name string (strcmp) and type byte against the query, returning the matching record or NULL.
Finds the cached player-stats record matching the current name/type, unlinks it from the record list and frees its associated parsed object.
Performs the cached player-stats record find/unlink/free sequence twice in a row to drop both the current and overall entries for the same name.
Parses an incoming player-stats reply, classifies it as current-game vs overall, replaces any prior cached record for that key, and refreshes the status text.
Builds a "get player stats" query with the selected player name and current/overall $TYPE and sends it to the server, then marks the request pending and refreshes the status text.
Stores a duplicated copy of the target player name (defaulting to a placeholder), selects current-game stats, and issues the stats request.
Allocates and lays out the stats-screen "Reload", "Current" and "Overall" buttons with their click callbacks and registers them with the UI list.
Initializes the player-stats screen layout globals, creates the scrolling text panel with its geometry and colors, and builds the screen buttons.
Formats the stats-screen title string with the current/overall label and player name, measures its width, and draws it horizontally centered.
Per-frame tick that fires the press/release handler for each hovered stats button and applies the hover-timeout state change on the scroll panel.
Parses a $-prefixed message-line directive token ($TYPE/$CTRL/$NAME/$TIME/$CATEGORY/$LABEL/$NEXT_COL), drawing control text or updating the chat-line render state globals accordingly.
Renders one chat message line, dispatching $-directives to the parser or drawing the sender name and message text into the proper column, then advances the vertical line cursor by the font height.
Resets the chat-render state then walks the linked list of message records, calling Chat_DrawMessageLine for each to draw the whole message log.
Releases the two embedded string members of a chat message record (at +4 and +0x10) under SEH and zeroes its first field, returning the record pointer.
Destroys the chat message store, freeing every node in its entry list (each with its two buffers) and tearing down its two member containers under SEH.
Walks the message store's entry list and returns the first record whose id field (+0xc) equals the requested id, or 0 if none match.
Counts message records whose category field (+8) matches the given value and returns true if that count has reached the per-category cap DAT_0067917c.
Selects a font/color-table slot based on whether the team value matches own or enemy team and returns its computed baseline pixel coordinate.
Chooses a font/color-table slot from the message mode (1, 2, or default) and team membership and returns its computed baseline pixel coordinate.
Computes the horizontal pixel position for a message by selecting a font slot from its team field and offsetting by full/half/quarter/three-quarter width per its category and alignment flag.
Renders one scoreboard player row (name, ping/tag, "%2d %4.2f" score column, and optional (dead)/uplink/cargo status lines via the font-draw vtable) and returns the row's pixel height.
Draws a team's scoreboard heading then walks the player-entry list calling Scoreboard_DrawPlayerRow for every entry belonging to that team, and marks the scoreboard surface dirty.
Binds the scoreboard font/surface globals, clears the overlay, and draws both team sections (DAT_005dd668 and DAT_005dd670) stacked vertically before marking the surface dirty.
When the detailed scoreboard is enabled, selects the team to show (DAT_00677f30: 1, 2, or other), draws its header, and renders each member row in detail mode via Scoreboard_DrawPlayerRow.
Allocates and constructs the two scoreboard manager objects (a 0x20-byte entry-list at DAT_00678390 and a 0x10-byte helper at DAT_00678394), storing null on allocation failure.

Ordering predicate for two scoreboard entries: ranks first by the per-type sort weight looked up in DAT_006783a4, then by the score fields at +0x30 and +0x28, returning nonzero when the first entry should sort ahead.
Inserts an entry into the scoreboard's sorted linked list, scanning with Scoreboard_CompareEntries to find its rank and splicing it at the head, after a node, or at the tail.
Re-sorts the entries chained off a list node by swapping out-of-order adjacent neighbors (using Scoreboard_CompareEntries) until stable, returning whether any swap occurred.

Allocates and initializes a 0x50-byte scoreboard entry, strdup's its name and team-tag strings, fills in player/score fields, links it into the global entry list, inserts it sorted, and refreshes the cached scoreboard surface.

Removes every scoreboard entry whose player id matches param_1: unlinks and frees the entry (and its name/tag strings), refreshes the surface, and also purges the player's nodes from the two auxiliary team lists.
Walks the player-entry list and, for every entry whose id at +0x10 matches the requested id, frees its old secondary-name string at +0x4 and replaces it with a strdup'd copy of the supplied name.
Walks the player-entry list and returns the player record whose slot id at +0x40 equals the requested value, or 0 if no entry matches.

Finds the player entry whose id at +0xc matches param_2 and writes the supplied stats fields into it (+0x10..+0x38) and its team at +0x8, announcing the local player's team name via chat when the team changes, then refreshes the scoreboard surface if dirty.
Finds the player entry whose id at +0xc matches param_2 and resets its state fields (state=2 at +0x3c, slot=-1 at +0x40, and clears the carried-cargo fields at +0x44/+0x48/+0x4c).

Case-insensitive comparison of two NUL-terminated strings over at most param_1 characters, returning the signed difference of the first differing lowercased characters (0 if equal), used for player-name matching.

Looks up a player by name prefix: returns the player id in *param_2 and true on an exact or single case-insensitive prefix match, and sets the ambiguous flag in *param_3 when more than one entry matches.

Finds the player entry whose id at +0xc matches param_2 and, for each non-null out-pointer, returns its name string (+0x0), team (+0x8) and secondary-name string (+0x4), returning true on success and 0 if no entry matches.
Walks the player-entry list tallying entries by their team id at +0x8 and returns the team-1 count in *param_1, the team-2 count in *param_2 and the neutral/team-0 count in *param_3.
Walks the player-entry list and returns the player record whose name string at +0x0 exactly matches the supplied name, or 0 if none matches.

Finds the player entry whose id at +0xc matches the given id and stores its carried-cargo flag (+0x44), cargo pointer (+0x48) and cargo value (+0x4c), then updates the local player's object-screen cargo display when the entry is the local player.
Allocates and zero-initializes the two name-string and two id linked-list heads of the name-completion table (loops i=0..1 building both the name list and id list for each category).

Resolves the given name to a unique id and, if found, appends the strdup'd name string and the resolved id into the completion-history name list and id list (selected by the boolean category flag) when not already present.

Counts the name-list entries matching the given prefix (case-insensitive) for the selected category; on a single match it completes the name and resolves/promotes its id, on multiple matches it sets the ambiguity flag, otherwise returns false.
Searches the selected category's name list for an exact (case-sensitive) name match and, when found, appends the given id to the paired id list if it is not already present.

Reads an effect-definition count then a stream of 0x18-byte records (id, double, two heap strings) into the freshly allocated DAT_006783a4 table, validating the count is in range 1..1999 and freeing strings on allocation failure.

Lazily initializes the default effect record then linearly scans the DAT_006783a4 effect table for the record whose id field matches the requested id, returning a pointer to its 6-dword entry (and setting the found flag) or the shared default record.

Sets the particle's RGB tint fields (+0xdc/+0xe0/+0xe4) to a default white, then overrides them to a red or blue team color when the owning entity is tintable and its base id matches the first or second team base.

Spawns an animated-sprite particle, builds a randomized velocity vector rotated by the supplied orientation angles and scaled by the global speed factors, writes it into the particle's velocity fields [5..7] and type field [0x1c], then applies the owner's team tint.
Spawns an animated-sprite particle, sets its type field [0x1c]=1 and its velocity fields [5..7] to the supplied direction vector scaled by the global speed factor, then applies the owner's team tint.

Spawns an animated-sprite particle (same effect template as Fx_SpawnDirectedParticle), sets type field [0x1c]=1 and velocity fields [5..7] to the supplied direction vector scaled by the global speed factor, then applies the owner's team tint.
Spawns a default-lifetime animated particle, tags it with effect type 2, and then runs the unit-destroyed debris/explosion emitter for the given entity.

Emits a type-specific burst of debris/secondary particles for a destroyed entity, then allocates and queues a fading explosion-light effect whose color, lifetime, and decay rate are chosen from the entity's type.
Picks a randomized particle count (rand modulo the given divisor plus a base offset) and emits that many particles via the generic effect emitter.
Spawns an animated particle with a type-dependent default lifetime and tags it with the effect type, skipping spawn for type 4 (smoke) when the source's measured value is below a culling threshold.

Allocates a 0x100-byte particle from a source position, scales its lifetime/size by the given factor, starts its sprite animation or sets a default texture, computes an animation LOD step from the frame delta, and links it into the active effect list.

Allocates a 0x100-byte quad effect particle whose center is the midpoint of two endpoints, stores the four corner offsets relative to that center, sets its random lifetime, and links it into the active effect list.

Builds a screen-facing beam between two endpoints by widening it along the normalized cross product of its direction and a view vector, then spawns two textured quad particles forming the beam's two halves.

Computes the start/end positions of one animated slice of a moving beam trail, clamps it against the beam's total length while deriving per-end texture-coordinate fractions, and spawns the corresponding beam segment.

Builds a normalized direction between two points and a view vector to the camera, computes how many trail slices to emit from the frame timing, and loops calling Fx_SpawnBeamTrailSlice to lay down a textured beam trail.

Builds a ground-level beam from an entity's position toward the camera, widens it along the normalized cross product of its direction and the view vector, and spawns two textured quad particles using the entity's team/owner texture index.
Spawns a type-9 animated effect particle, stores the three given vector components and a per-frame update callback (LAB_004768a0) on it.
Builds two textured billboard beam-segment quads from two basis direction vectors, width/length scale factors, and computed UV coordinates.
Computes a unit's engine-exhaust emitter point in world space, transforms its direction basis, and emits the beam quads forming the thrust/exhaust trail when above the speed threshold.
