Dispatches on the effect-kind code in EAX (0-4) to spawn the corresponding particle, random burst, or thrust-trail effect.

Builds the entity's orientation matrix from its Euler angles, projects it into the spatial grid, and submits the resulting sprite/decal to the draw queue or contact index, then restores the original orientation.
Temporarily forces the active draw context's render mode to 5, builds the entity orientation matrix, projects and submits the sprite/decal, then restores the render mode and orientation.
Projects the entity with its orientation angles zeroed (axis-aligned) into the spatial grid and submits the resulting sprite/decal to the draw queue or contact index.
Projects the entity position and its scaled velocity to screen space and stores the atan2 screen-space heading angle (plus a bias) into the entity's rotation field at +0x2c.
Advances all contrails and effect particles for the elapsed frame time: integrates position, applies gravity/drag, runs expiry callbacks, and frees dead particles.
Picks a sprite index from one of two effect tables based on the entity's type and a frame-counter cycle, then spawns a type-0xc animated particle showing it.

Builds the camera billboard basis, computes the frame delta-time, then walks the active projectile list and dispatches each entry by its type to set the render mode and call the matching per-type update/draw handler.

Creates the active projectile list and resolves all weapon-effect texture handles by name (fire, gunblast, shot, and red/blue light sprites), forcing them to mip level zero and preloading the light textures.
Zeroes a projectile-effect object's position, velocity, and timer fields, sets its three scale components to 1.0, and assigns its default type code 0xc.
Walks and frees the projectile list, the contrail list (releasing each contrail's segments), and the smoke-trail list, then clears all three list headers.
Iterates the projectile list and adds a fading lens-flare transient for each muzzle-flash entry, then iterates the world entity list adding contrail and glow draws for the matching entity types.
Computes the start and end points of a projectile's motion beam, clips it against geometry, normalizes the direction, and emits a fixed number of stepped trail segments along it.
Allocates and constructs the global profanity-filter object, storing the result (or null on allocation failure) in the singleton pointer.
Initializes a profanity-filter object with the file-system base, duplicates the "profanity.txt" filename, creates its word list, and loads the word list from the file.
Opens the profanity word file and reads it line by line, skipping blank and comment lines, then duplicates each leading token and appends it to the filter's word list.
Walks the filter's word list, freeing each node's duplicated string payload and unlinking the node from the list.
Duplicates both strings, upper-cases them, runs strstr to find the needle in the haystack case-insensitively, and returns a pointer into the original haystack at the match (or NULL).
Walks the banned-word list and overwrites every case-insensitive occurrence of each banned word in the given string with asterisks ('*'), returning the same string.

Tests whether the entity is a valid lockable target by checking its team/type/flags, that its bearing from the camera falls within the current zoom field-of-view (dot vs sin threshold), and that the viewer has line of sight to it.
Looks up a palette color via the direction-index tables, marshals the line endpoints through the float-to-fixed helper, and issues the renderer's draw-line vtable call (+0x94) in that color.
Transforms the forward vector by the view matrix and scans the 8 compass-direction sin/cos table entries, returning the index of the direction whose dot product with the view forward is largest.
Computes sin/cos of the given angle and emits three draw-primitive vtable calls (+0x70) to render an arc/segment of the compass ring.

Computes sin/cos of the given angle, marshals the resulting endpoint coordinates through the float-to-fixed helper, and issues one draw-primitive vtable call (+0x70) to render a single compass spoke/segment.
Draws the full HUD compass ring by rendering the base arc once and then seven spokes/segments, all in the shared compass color.
If the map panel is active, iterates every cell of the 2D grid clearing its first three state bytes and freeing each cell's allocated buffer back to the pool, then resets any active drag state.

Scans all world object slots and their three sub-entries to find the maximum object height/radius value (field +0x28), then stores that maximum plus a fixed margin into the global tallest-object cache.
Recomputes the cached max terrain height if dirty, then spawns a callback marker particle at the given grid cell's world position and stores its handle in the cell.
Spawns a fade-out effect at the given grid cell's world position and detaches the cell's existing marker particle by redirecting its callback and clearing the cell handle.
Applies a bitmask of state flags to the grid cell at the given row/column, spawning or releasing marker particles to match, then resets any active map-panel drag.
Allocates the rows-by-columns 2D grid of map-panel cell structs, zeroes each cell's marker handle, and resets the panel state.
Computes an animated pulse/oscillation scalar from the current millisecond timer modulo 500, used to animate map-panel markers.
Computes the distance from a candidate's screen position to the pick point and, if closer than the current best, records it as the nearest picked object.
Draws a unit's blip on the map panel via the renderer vtable, scaling its size by the panel zoom and selecting the blip color based on the unit's team flag.
Transforms a unit's world position into the map panel's local frame and computes its on-panel x/y screen coordinates plus the rotated offset vector.
Computes a unit's map-panel screen position, draws its blip, and, when picking is active, tests it as a nearest-pick candidate.
Initializes the nearest-object pick state for the map panel, storing the click position relative to the panel and resetting the best-distance and picked-object to defaults.
Projects a world-space point through the map-view matrix, converts it to a map-screen X coordinate using the world-to-map scale and origin, and invokes the renderer's vtable+0xB0 point-draw entry.
Stores the new map zoom scale and recomputes the map origin, extents, and per-cell step globals from the current view transform, then rebuilds the map cell grid.

Converts the two input world coordinates to integer grid-cell indices, clamps each to the valid [0, gridDim-1] range, and writes the column index to the EDI out-pointer and the row index to the EBX out-pointer.

Validates the (col,row) grid coordinate, and if in bounds reads the cell's two data bytes into globals and builds a two-character grid label ('a'+col, '1'+row), returning the label pointer or NULL when out of bounds.
Allocates the next sprite object from the token stream, forces its type field to 3, runs the sprite-setup helper, sets the load/keep flag bits 0x42, and returns the object's slot id.

Builds the 256x256 map-overview snapshot by allocating four sprite buffers, rendering the elevation/relief/object passes, then copying and palette-tinting the result and downsampling each sprite buffer for display.
Walks the linked list of active map pings, advances each by the elapsed time (updating its animated value and replotting it), and unlinks/frees any ping whose remaining lifetime has expired.
Returns the map blip color code for the entity's team, choosing 0x0F for the local/friendly team, 0x0B for the enemy team, and 1 for all other teams.

Draws one entity on the map: caches the local player's screen position as a special case, otherwise projects the entity to map space and renders it either as a movable-unit marker or as a static object icon.
Selects the map blip color index and scale for an entity based on its type and team, applies a dimming factor when the overview mode is active, and returns whether the entity should be drawn at all.

Builds a world-space vertex from the given X/Z (with the shared Y from _DAT_00564f08), transforms it by the active overlay matrix and projects it to screen space, then stores the position and projected coordinates into the current quad vertex slot.

Builds a ground-relative vertex from the given X/Z by subtracting the world origin offsets (_DAT_005e65d0/d8/e0 and the level base height), projects it to screen space, and stores the position and projected coordinates into the current quad vertex slot.

Sets up the camera view pose and overlay transform, fills the four quad vertices (with per-corner texture coordinates and colors) by projecting the four ground corners, optionally clips the quad against a plane, draws it with the given texture mode, and restores the view transform.
Convenience wrapper that draws a ground overlay quad via MapOverlay_DrawGroundQuad using opaque white vertex colors and zero texture coordinates.

Initializes the four quad vertices with default white colors, projects four transformed corners via MapOverlay_EmitTransformedVertex, optionally clips the quad against a plane, and draws it with the given texture handle and mode.
Builds an axis-aligned rectangle from two opposite corners and draws it as a transformed overlay quad, selecting blend mode 'e'/0x65 (additive) when the flag is set or 'a'/0x61 otherwise.
Unprojects the given screen-space X/Y through the viewport to recover a world ground point and stores it as a homogeneous (x, 1.0, z) triple in the output vertex.
Unprojects two screen-space endpoints (offset by the viewport origin) to world points and builds a normalized plane through them via Plane_BuildFromThreePoints.

Sets the render target and clip planes, configures the camera view pose, and tiles the active map view buffer across a 2x2 grid of overlay rectangles (clipping the center seam) before restoring the view transform.
Sets the render target and clip planes, configures the camera view pose, and draws the active map view buffer as a single full-extent overlay rectangle before restoring the view transform.
Per-object map/radar draw callback that picks the blip color and style for one entity, drawing it as a colored marker, icon, or scaled sprite based on its type and visibility/lock state.

Renders a full radar/map frame: computes the map scale, sets the target buffer and clip planes, builds the view frustum planes, enumerates all objects drawing each blip, then overlays the compass tick, target cone wedge, and selection highlight.
Draws the map's terrain grid: projects the X/Y grid line coordinates, renders the terrain elevation grid, plots clipped grid cross-marks, then draws the four border edges in the cached palette color.
Maps the current compass heading and pitch into normalized screen X/Y outputs by linearly interpolating them between the given source ranges and destination spans.
Clears the selection flag and renders the inset map terrain view using the view rectangle extents (offsets 0x14-0x20) scaled by the current map zoom factor.

Draws the glow pass for all map objects, restores the target selection if one was pending, and finalizes the inset map frame by mapping the compass value to screen coordinates and clearing the dirty flag.
Top-level inset-map renderer that, when a player view exists, computes the map scale and runs the terrain view, terrain-grid, and glow/finalize passes in sequence.
Rounds a pair of floating-point projected coordinates to integer screen X and Y and stores them through the two output pointers.

Draws a colored triangular heading marker for an object on the map by rotating three local offset vectors into the object's world position, projecting them to screen, and stroking the three edges in the given color.
Initializes an input/event node and stores the given value into its first field while clearing the node's flag byte.
Initializes the radar overlay: computes a scaled clock interval, allocates three radar list objects, loads each radar icon bitmap by name, and normalizes its per-icon direction vector pair.

Lazily runs radar icon-table init once, evaluates each registered radar-blip callback into the output float array, computes a 20-step clock-based blink phase, and draws the radar with a temporary render mode.
Frees the network update-array's 2D cell grid, clearing each referenced entity's back-pointer/flag fields before releasing the row buffers and the grid itself.

Reads a bit-width-prefixed field set from the network bitstream for the indexed entry, optionally advances the running position/value accumulators, and decodes three dequantized RGB-style float components into the output pointers.
Reads one bit-width-prefixed field from the network bitstream and returns its dequantized float value for the current update-array entry.
Walks the unit's eligible weapon/turret slots and, per bit of the supplied mask, sets or clears the corresponding entry's active flag (clearing its timer when deactivated).
Decodes the four bitmask-gated turret/weapon sub-update sections (firing, active, deploy, and ammo) from the network bitstream into the target unit's per-slot state array.

Applies a decoded object update record to an entity, copying position/orientation, activating or spawning it, handling local-player ack-wait and parent-vehicle reassignment, then advances the tick and frees the record.

If the presence bit is set, decodes the local vehicle's chassis type, throttle and turn floats, terrain index, and optional altitude/secondary values from the network bitstream into the output state record.
If the update sequence is newer than the last applied, writes the decoded throttle/fuel-scaled drive values, optional altitude fields, and turret mask onto the local player's vehicle and HUD state.

Copies the source snapshot's position (+0x20..+0x28) and orientation (+0x38..+0x40) into the interpolation record when the corresponding valid flags (+0x50/+0x52) are set, otherwise zeroes the velocity/derivative slots.

Decodes an incoming world-state snapshot packet, looking up or creating each referenced unit, applying its position/orientation/health/fuel/target fields, advancing interpolation, and replying to server pings.
Formats the given (or last) Win32 error code into a static text buffer via FormatMessageA, falling back to a sprintf placeholder string when formatting fails, and returns the buffer.
Writes a null-terminated string as a REG_SZ value under the object's open registry key, printing a detailed error message to stderr if RegSetValueExA fails.
Reads the "Location" REG_SZ value from the object's registry key, duplicates it via strdup into the caller's out-pointer, and returns true only when the read succeeds with a string type.
Flushes the object's open registry key to disk with RegFlushKey and then releases the associated key-path buffer.
Appends the named subkey to the object's registry path and opens it, creating it if absent, showing an error MessageBox and aborting if neither open nor create succeeds.
Reads the registry "Location" string and stores it in the out-pointer, but treats the placeholder "<NOT SET>" as no value by freeing it and storing null, also writing a default when the query fails.
Computes the vector from the first point to the second into the ESI result and applies successive Z/Y/X axis rotations to convert that direction into oriented angle components.

Reserves space in the frame command buffer for a render node and its per-vertex array, zero-fills the array, links the node into the global list, and returns success unless the source mesh has no data.

Walks the parent node's child-object linked list, computes each child's position relative to the node origin, builds its plane-test vector, and re-inserts it into the spatial tree leaf via MapBsp_InsertObjectIntoLeaf.
Reserves a 0x68-byte map render node from the frame arena pool (DAT_005ba078), advancing the bump pointer and zeroing the new node's link and state fields.

Transforms a terrain quad's four corners through the active view matrix, perspective-projects them to screen-space using the viewport scale and offset globals, stores the results in the clip-plane scratch state, and classifies the quad's screen area for LOD selection.

Dispatches rendering of a map node by its type field (+0x14): type 3 enqueues a callback command, type 2 projects/classifies a quad, otherwise it rebins child objects and recurses, then advances the per-frame node bucket pointer.

Descends the terrain BSP tree, testing the object position against each node's split plane to pick the front/back child, and links the object into the destination leaf's per-cell object bucket (merging if the same root already present).

Sutherland-Hodgman clip of a vertex fan against a single plane, emitting kept vertices and interpolating new edge-crossing vertices (position, texcoords, and re-projected screen coordinates) into the output buffer and writing the output count.

Clips a polygon against every active view-frustum plane (selected by OR-ing the per-vertex outcodes), ping-ponging between two scratch vertex buffers and bailing out as soon as the polygon is fully culled.
Clips a polygon successively against each plane in a map node's plane list, ping-ponging two scratch vertex buffers, or copies the four input vertices through unchanged when the node has no planes.

Classifies up to 32 fan vertices against the clip volume, trivially rejecting or accepting via the AND/OR of their outcodes, clips when straddling, and appends the surviving fan to the map draw queue while reporting whether anything was emitted.

Classifies up to 32 polygon vertices against the full clip volume, trivially rejecting or clipping as needed, and forwards the resulting polygon to the renderer through the device vtable draw method at offset 0xa8.

Gathers per-vertex texture/color attributes from a vertex array via a u16 index list (clamped to 32), builds the scratch pointer table, and emits the polygon as a textured/gouraud fan via Map_DrawQueueFan.
Gathers per-vertex position/color attributes from a vertex array via a u16 index list, builds the scratch pointer table, and emits the polygon as a flat-shaded fan via MapDrawQueue_AppendClippedFan.

Recursively walks the map BSP tree in back-to-front order relative to the eye, drawing each node's polygons via the fan emitters and releasing the node's deferred draw-record lists by decrementing their refcounts.
Iterates the model's flat face list, back-face/plane culls each face against the eye, and emits the visible ones through the textured or flat fan emitter.
Sets up the model transform, projects all of its vertices to screen space, then renders it either by BSP traversal or by linear face-list draw depending on the BSP-present flag.
Tests a point against the view frustum clip-plane set, returning 0 if it lies fully behind the near radius and otherwise outputting the bitmask of planes the point crosses.

Allocates and initializes a 0x68-byte sprite/billboard draw-command record (from the recycle pool when an attached emitter qualifies, otherwise from the frame arena) filling its position, color, and size fields.
Allocates a 0x68-byte type-2 draw-command record from the frame arena and initializes it with a position and size copied from a referenced source object.
Transforms a world point into view space, clip-tests it, and on success allocates a sprite draw command and stores the point's view-space position into it.
Transforms a world point into view space, clip-tests it, and on success allocates a sprite draw command and stores the point's position plus a color/extra vector and size into it.

Transforms an entity's world position into view space, tests it against the shadow clip-plane set, and on success allocates and fills a shadow-projection record (position, orientation, radius, source entity/model) from the shadow pool.

Transforms a light/volume position into view space, tests it against the shadow clip-plane set, allocates and fills a shadow record, and when the flag is set writes a signed orientation basis back into the source object.
Allocates and constructs the global shadow manager (0xac0 bytes), seeds its head list node, and creates the 0x10000-byte block-allocator arena used to pool shadow records.
Initializes the shadow manager object: sets up its clip-plane state, allocates a large (0x5bec) scratch buffer, and zeroes the record/count fields of the structure.
Clamps a 1D interval (low/high in EBX/EDI) to the inclusive bounds [ESI,param_1], writing back the clamped endpoints and returning false if the interval lies fully outside.

Clips a 2D rectangle (origin EAX/param_1, extents param_3/param_4) against a region's min/max bounds, returning the visible offsets, clipped origin and clipped extents through the optional out-pointers, or false if fully outside.

Builds the per-triangle shadow projection/interpolation matrix from three vertices, computing the edge determinant (clearing the valid flag and bailing if degenerate) and the screen-space and depth gradient coefficients.
Allocates a 4-field shadow-caster list node initialized with the source object and its model handle, and attaches a freshly constructed sub-list helper.

Computes a shadow caster's world-space origin and projection axis by transforming the model's offset vector through the object's cached Euler rotation matrix and adding the object position, storing the result into the output record.
Extends the shadow caster's origin along its projection axis to a far endpoint and clips that ray against the terrain, replacing the endpoint with the intersection point when the ray hits.
Advances the shock-beam node's two double phase accumulators by the per-frame time delta according to its mode field and wraps each back to 0 when it passes 1.0.

Advances the beam phase, interpolates the segment endpoints, builds a normalized perpendicular offset scaled by beam width, and spawns two red/blue shock quad particles, returning true when the node should be removed.
Frees a shock-effect node: releases its bolt buffer, walks its child-segment list freeing each payload, then tears down and frees the child list container.

Ensures a beam emitter exists for the given entity id: reuses the current one if it matches, otherwise destroys it and allocates a fresh 0x40 emitter initialized from the entity's transform/object lookup.
Walks the global shock-effect list and deactivates every node owned by the given entity id, tearing down each node's emitter and clearing its active flag.
Initializes the shock-effect subsystem by resolving the shockred001/shockblue001 texture indices and allocating the global shock-node list.
Iterates the global shock-effect list each frame, validating the owning entity, refreshing emitter transforms, spawning beam quads, and pruning dead nodes and child segments.
Returns the scoreboard column X coordinate for the given message-type code by reading the matching field of the HUD layout table.
Computes the scoreboard text X position for a chat/score message by matching its kudos/endorses prefix or its type/subtype fields against the HUD layout table columns.
Returns the low-byte scoreboard column position for a message based on its type field at offset 0x20, reading the matching column from the HUD layout table.
Renders one text segment of a chat message into the chat-log document viewer, prefixing the sender name(s) and choosing the text color by message type, then reflows the log and trims it to 100 lines.
Splits a chat message node's text on newline and NUL boundaries and appends each resulting line to the chat log via Chat_AppendMessageLine.
Frees a chat message node's text and sender-name strings (offsets 0, 6 and 7) and then the node itself.
Plays an alert sound for an incoming chat message when it is a same-team chat or a "Distress" message and the local message-sound entity is active.

Builds a chat message node (handling the "16309 " remote-command prefix, banned-word censoring, and player-name lookup), plays its alert, appends it to the 100-entry message ring buffer, and renders it into the chat log.
Selects the chat-log font/palette resource according to the local team flag and applies it to the chat-log document viewer when the team has changed.

Builds the chat-log UI: initializes the chat controller and palette, allocates the comm entry, document viewer, Package_LR/Package_TB containers and scrollbar, wires them together, replays any saved log line, and resolves the named team color indices.
Formats the "Message (to %s):" chat input prompt and draws it right-aligned above the input box using the chat controller's renderer.
Constructs a Comm_Entry chat-controller widget, initializing its base fields and allocating its child Text_Entry input control.
Computes the pixel height of the chat input box from the number of wrapped text lines, the line height and the border padding.
Builds the current chat prompt/state and invokes the console widget's draw method to render the prompt line at its computed height.
When the console line at param_1 has content, measures the text, computes its screen position, and draws a highlighted/selected entry rectangle via the console's draw object.
Draws the console prompt line then fills the team-colored background and input-area bars across the screen, updating the cursor-blink toggle flag.
Clears the console screen rectangle, frees the active markup document and its buffer, and walks the line list freeing each node before invoking the layout object's cleanup method.
Reallocates the save buffer to fit two screen rows if needed, then copies the top two pixel rows from the framebuffer into the buffer so the area under the console can later be restored.
Copies the two saved pixel rows from the save buffer back into the top two rows of the framebuffer, restoring the screen area previously hidden by the console.
Per-frame console update that handles screen-resize re-save, restores or redraws the overlay, draws the background bars, and applies the team-shaded colors to the layout's color slots.
Returns the default palette entry's base color reduced by its scaled shade value (rounded), producing a darkened console color index.
Selects the palette entry for the team owning the given object (or the default), and returns its base color minus a scaled shade value OR'd with 0x0c00 as a console color word.

Selects the palette entry for the team owning the given object (or the default) and returns its base color minus a differently-scaled shade value OR'd with 0x0c00, a brighter variant of the team console color word.
Maps a team id to its scoreboard column index by comparing it against the two registered team objects' ids at +0x18, returning the matching team's id or the opposing one.
Resolves the scoreboard team-column index for the entity in EAX by comparing its team id at +0xf0 against the two registered team objects' ids.
Adds one entity's resource value into the per-team resource totals and bumps the per-team unit counts, special-casing type 0xd to the opposing team's column.
Walks the scoreboard row list and, per row type, animates each row's count and per-team value fields toward the freshly computed resource/count totals scaled by the row's interpolation rate.
Zeroes every scoreboard row's count/value display fields and resets all per-team resource and unit-count accumulator globals to zero before a fresh recompute.
Clears the accumulators then walks every live entity, tallying its resources and per-row unit counts into the team scoreboard rows and summing the grand totals.
While in game mode 2, counts down a refresh timer and, when it expires or a forced refresh is requested, resets the timer and recomputes the team resource totals.
Allocates fifteen zero-initialized scoreboard row nodes, each tagged with a resource/unit type id and label string, and appends them to the team-resources row list.
Initializes the team-resources HUD panel by building its row list, setting the panel rectangle and layout columns, creating the scroller, and loading the team_resources_skeleton model.
Draws the "Team" and "Resources" column header strings into the team-resources HUD panel via the renderer's text-draw vtable entry, right-aligning each by its measured width.
Draws the resource panel's right-aligned header by measuring and rendering the active team's name string and the "Resources" label.
Renders the resource table panel: prints a no-team message if none is selected, otherwise draws the Resource/Count/Percent column headers and one formatted row per resource from the active list.
Measures the sprintf scratch buffer string and draws it right-aligned against column 0x41 at the given row and color.
Draws one team's resource-summary column at the given x offset: the team name, a two-pixel underline bar, the numeric resource Value, and (if applicable) the Percent line.
Draws the "Resource Summary" title and divider bar, then renders the summary column for each of the three teams ordered by which team is the local player's.
Frees the resource-graph buffer by releasing each row's two data arrays then the row array itself and nulls the global pointer.
Allocates the resource-graph buffer as a row array of 32-byte entries, each holding two sample arrays initialized to a default value and zeroed counters.
Frees any existing resource-graph buffer and, if more than one resource is tracked, reallocates it and resets all graph state counters, returning success.
Handles the resource panel's key/event type 0xd by resetting transient action-state slots and either applying display settings or entering the saved major mode.
No-op event/callback stub that always returns 0.
Switches to the in-game screen mode (3) and, if the HELLO handshake has not yet completed, sends the final HELLO-complete packet to join the session.
Allocates and initializes the route-test screen mode object, wiring its input/draw vtable handlers and registering its enter/exit callbacks in the screen-mode table.
Renders the route-latency test screen, drawing each route's label and per-sample timing values, highlighting the lowest-latency route, and printing the best route found so far.
Stores the current high-resolution timestamp into the route-ping matrix cell for the given route index and sample slot, bounds-checked against the route and sample counts.
On each timer interval, sends a ROUTING_PING to every route for the current sample slot, advances the slot/round counters, and finishes the test once all sample slots are sent.
Optionally sets the login status-line text, switches to the login screen mode (2), and performs a full session reset/disconnect.
Lazily creates the "enter the Internet address of a game server" text-entry dialog, sets its prompt strings, and copies the supplied initial address text into its input buffer.
Input handler for the login screen mode: on an unmodified Enter key, resets transient action-slot state and either reapplies display settings or enters the major mode.
Allocates and initializes the login screen mode object, wiring its key-event/draw vtable handlers and registering its enter/exit callbacks in the screen-mode table.
Thin wrapper that builds the stripmap (route-overview map) texture geometry by delegating to the stripmap mesh-build routine.
Copies the current display/render configuration (driver pointer, palettes, gamma, fog, texture/allocator callbacks, and antialias settings) into the active renderer state globals at 0x5f55b0.
Queries the active display driver's name and posts a "Display system active: <name>." status line to the chat/console.
Lazily allocates the three HUD font-descriptor blocks and, when running at low resolution, copies the lores font descriptors into the active small/options font slots.
Builds the HUD font glyph descriptors from named texture entries and loads/preloads all HUD animation sequences (arrows, flags, warp, trails, mouse pointer).
Recomputes the antialias/supersample enable flag from the gamma and driver capability settings, then re-syncs the renderer driver state.
When the requested resolution differs, logs the resolution switch, asks the driver to change mode, then re-derives the lores flag and reinitializes viewports, fonts, and HUD layout.
Recomputes the antialias enable flag, re-syncs renderer state, then applies any pending resolution switch.
Installs the given display driver, initializes it, queries the screen dimensions, and allocates and registers the six render viewport/target descriptors scaled for the current resolution.
Disables the optional overlay device, re-syncs renderer state, calls the driver's shutdown vtable slot, and clears the active-context flag.

Tears down the current display driver and brings up the requested one (initializing viewports on first use or re-applying resolution, fonts, fog, and overlay state otherwise), returning whether the switch succeeded.
Queries the current display mode from the render device, refreshes all surface contexts for the new resolution, and reapplies the viewport clip rectangle.
Lazily creates the two global file-search-path lists and populates both with the default data, docs, maps, sound, and client bitmap directories.
Registers a labeled bucket for every network packet-type id (ROOT, PING, PLAYER, TANK, etc.) into a histogram widget and finalizes it with the given title and scale.
Toggles the network packet-count and packet-size debug histogram overlay on or off, lazily constructing and positioning the two histogram widgets the first time it is shown.
Draws the console/dialogue panel background by tiling the lazily-loaded "brown/20" border texture around the edges and stroking the inner and outer bevel lines.
Clears the console text widget, frees its current and backing markup documents, and replaces the backing buffer with a fresh empty rich-text document.
Renders the console overlay: scrolls the panel, draws the text document and background frame, and centers the "Server Shutdown!" banner across the screen.
Lazily constructs the console scrolling text widget, positions it within the screen margins, and seeds it with the current default font.

Builds the console/help screen: allocates its callback object and Viewer, wires its render and event vtable slots, creates its text widget, and registers the "main_menu" and "command_dialogue" search namespaces.
Opens or closes the console overlay: on open it stores a duplicated message string and switches to the console screen mode, on close it returns to the gameplay screen mode.
Computes the sky-dust billboard right/up axis vectors from the given rotation angle via sin/cos scaling and normalizes them into the global dust orientation vectors.
On first call seeds 500 random dust-particle positions and colors, then projects each particle to screen space and plots its colored pixel if it lies within the viewport.
Constructs a scrolling-text panel object, initializing its two chunk linked lists and default size/speed/color fields, then resets it via TextScroller_Reset.
Splits an input string into width-limited segments breaking at spaces and appends each segment to the scroller as a text chunk via TextScroller_AddChunk.
Allocates a text-chunk node copying the given string, font, and color, links it into the scroller's chunk list, and advances the running character and pixel-width totals.
Frees all queued text chunks and glow-track nodes in the scroller's two lists, releases their buffers, and zeroes the scroller's counters and timer back to the default tick interval.

Walks the scroller's pending chunk list and draws each chunk's text up to the current reveal-character count, computing a brightness-shaded color per chunk and stopping once the visible-character budget is exhausted.
Iterates the active glow-character list, drawing each character at a FloatTrack-driven fading brightness and removing and freeing the node once its glow track has finished.
Finds the chunk containing the next character to reveal, allocates a glow-character node with its screen position and a new FloatTrack fade animation, and appends it to the active glow list.
Advances the scroller by the elapsed frame time, draws the visible and glowing characters, and spawns one new glow character per due tick until all queued text has been revealed.
Scalar deleting destructor for a sound voice: runs the voice destructor and frees the object when the low bit of the flags argument is set.

Maps an entity's type code (field +8) to the sound-effect id to play, gated on the active listener, a global sound-enable flag, and per-entity audible flags, returning 1 when no special sound applies.
Returns 1.0 when there is no active listener, otherwise returns a float scale derived from the listener state.

Recomputes a voice's distance-based volume against its source's min/max range, enforces the per-sound concurrent-voice limit, and stops/frees the voice (or its quietest duplicate) when out of range or over the limit.
Constructs a Sound_Player: installs its vftable, initializes the sound-definition and voice list members, and sets the default channel count and active flag.

Opens base_sound\\index.wgn, parses each non-comment line into a Sound_Def (name, file, gains, ranges, flags), assigns it an id, appends it to the player's definition list, and asks the audio backend to preload the referenced sample.
Walks the sound-definition linked list looking for the entry whose name matches the given string and returns that Sound_Def, or null if none match.
Walks the active voice list and returns the first voice whose sound-def id matches param_2 and whose owning entity matches the searched entity, or 0 if none.
Stops every active voice that references the given Sound_Def, unlinks the def from the player's definition list, and frees the def's name, file string, and the def itself.
Stops and releases every active voice, then asks the audio backend to free and deletes each Sound_Def, and finally clears the player's definition list.
Sound_Player destructor: installs the vftable then tears down the two embedded voice/bank linked-list members.
Searches the active-voice list for the voice whose handle (+0x3c) equals the requested id and invokes the vtable stop-voice method on it.
Walks the active-voice list and stops every unattached voice whose sound-definition type matches the given type id.

Plays a positional sound by allocating and initializing a voice node, filling its position/source/priority fields, assigning a new handle, and submitting it to the mixer, returning the handle or -1 on failure.
Plays a sound attached to an emitter object by allocating a voice node, setting its source-object and attached flag, assigning a new handle, and submitting it, returning the handle or -1 on failure.
Per-frame sound tick: decays the global volume ramp, runs the listener update, then walks every active voice applying expiry, re-evaluation, and freeing finished or stopped voices.
Looks up the sound-definition's playback length for the type and, if enough time has elapsed since the last play, calls the update-or-spawn routine to (re)start the sound.
Per-frame entity-sound sync: flags looping voices for refresh, then walks every world entity, computes its current sound type, and triggers the matching one-shot voice.
Updates the matching active voice's position/velocity if one already exists, otherwise allocates a new looping voice with a type-specific timeout and submits it when the priority threshold is met.
Stops the active voice of the given type, or when the enable flag is set instead spawns a new looping voice of that type if none is already playing.
Walks the sound manager's active-voice list and invokes the stop/free vtable method on every voice whose source entity matches the given entity.
Zero-initializes a 0x60-byte sound-voice structure, presetting the gain field (+0x34) to 1.0 and the two id fields (+0x3c/+0x40) to -1.
Returns the squared distance from a sound voice's world position to the listener, accounting for the voice's attached entity transform, or 0 if the voice is 2D or no listener exists.
Enables the sound system by calling the manager's enable vtable method with 1 and setting the manager's audio-enabled flag (+8) to true.
Disables the sound system by calling the manager's enable vtable method with 0 and clearing the manager's audio-enabled flag (+8).
If audio is enabled and the sound id is valid, spawns a 3D positional voice for the given sound id at the supplied world coordinates.
If audio is enabled and the sound id is valid, spawns a 3D voice attached to the given entity (defaulting to the listener when null) with an entity-relative offset.
If audio is enabled and the sound id is valid, spawns a non-positional (2D/UI) voice for the given sound id with the supplied gain and pitch.
If audio is enabled, plays the fixed UI sound id 0x19 as a 2D voice at the globally configured click gain.
If audio is enabled, plays the fixed UI sound id 0x1a as a 2D voice at full gain (1.0).
If the effects manager exists and is active, spawns effect type 0x64 at full intensity (1.0) as a one-shot transient effect.

When enabled, spawns a looping effect (type 0x47, or 0x66 in chase/external view) at intensity _DAT_00679278 unless one is already present, recording its id in DAT_005b9058; when disabled, despawns the recorded effect.
Per-frame tick that derives whether the engine glow should be on from the game/player state, toggles that looping effect accordingly, and then advances the whole effect emitter manager.
Walks every node in the effect manager's emitter list and invokes the manager's kill-emitter vtable method (offset 0x5c) on each, tearing down all active effect emitters.

Maps an object/event type code (EAX) to a specific effect-type id via a switch and spawns that transient effect at the supplied position, when the effects manager and world are active and effects are not suppressed.
Under SEH protection, zero-initializes a temporary 3-word effect record on the stack and passes it to FUN_0052a350 for processing before unwinding.
For an entity with a model definition, copies its primary offset vec3 and, if an emitter is active or the model's flag at +5 is set, fires the distance-attenuated sound/effect at that position.

Synchronizes an entity's looping effect with its model state: copies the primary offset, then spawns the looping effect (type 1, or 0x6a in alternate mode) when its flag at +0x15 is set and none exists, or despawns the existing one when the flag is clear.
Rotates the vec3 in ESI sequentially about the X, Y, and Z axes by calling the single-axis rotation helper with axis codes 1, 2, and 3.
Loads an FSOUND sample, reads its mode/length to size and allocate a PCM buffer, locks the sample to copy its decoded audio into that buffer, then unlocks and frees the FSOUND sample, returning true.

Parses a time string in HH:MM:SS.f, MM:SS.f, or plain-seconds form via sscanf, converts it to a rounded sample/frame offset using the source's sample-rate and frame-size fields, and stores the result through the output pointer.
Parses the start and end timecodes of a clip and returns true only when both parse successfully and the resulting sample offsets form a valid in-bounds range within the source length.
Initializes a sound stream-reader cursor, clearing its position/flags and seeding the loop start and end sample offsets from the bound source object when one is provided.

Copies the requested number of bytes into the destination from the source sample buffer, wrapping the read cursor back to the loop start whenever it reaches the loop end so playback repeats seamlessly.

Copies up to the requested bytes from the source buffer into the destination without looping, zero-fills any remainder past the end of the sample data, and returns true once the cursor has reached the end of the source.

Fills the destination buffer from a stream reader, optionally rewinding the cursor first, dispatching to the looping or one-shot read path based on the reader's loop flag and returning whether more data remains.
Lazily creates the global Sound_fmod singleton by allocating a 0x50-byte object and constructing it on first use, then returns the cached instance.
Constructs a Sound_fmod object by running the base Sound_Player constructor, installing the Sound_fmod vftable, and initializing its default volume, gain, and channel-count fields.
Scalar deleting destructor for Sound_fmod that runs the destructor and then frees the object's memory when the low bit of the flag argument is set.
Destructor for Sound_fmod that releases the object's FMOD samples and record buffers then chains to the base Sound_Player destructor.

Allocates a 0x1c sound-sample struct, runs the custom decode/load passes, and on success stores it at sample+0x44 with data-type tag 1 (custom) at sample+0x40, freeing everything and returning false on failure.
Frees the inner PCM buffer pointed to by the custom sample struct and then frees the struct itself.

Searches a list of candidate sound directory/extension suffixes, builds the full path, and loads the sample via FSOUND_Sample_Load (with looping/hardware flags) or the custom loader, logging an error if no file could be loaded.
Releases a loaded sample based on its data-type tag at +0x40 (FSOUND_Sample_Free for type 0, custom struct free for type 1, error log otherwise) and clears the sample pointer.

Builds the FSOUND 3D position and velocity vectors for a sound source from its attached object's transform, subtracting the listener origin and rotating into the editor view frame, returning zero vectors when the source is muted.

Updates one playing sound source: distance-culls it, computes a time/distance volume rolloff, applies FSOUND volume and 3D attributes, emits a debug entry, and returns false (stopping the source) if any FSOUND call fails.

Once per frame-tick, walks the active sound-source list updating each audible in-range source via Snd_UpdateSourcePlayback (stopping failed ones), calls FSOUND_Update, then recomputes each source's audibility flag.
Stores the given parent/attach object pointer at source+0x28 (the transform source used for 3D attribute computation) and returns true.
Returns the source base volume at +0x28 scaled by the global master-attenuation factor (1 - masterVol*muteFactor).
Forwards the source and its parameters to the channel-start helper (FUN_0048ba10) to begin playback and returns true.
No-op stdcall stub (RET 8) installed in a sound-device vtable slot that takes one argument and does nothing.
Enumerates the FMOD sound drivers, building a driver-info record (name plus a capabilities suffix for hardware 3D and EAX2/EAX3 support) for each and appending it to the global driver list.

Initializes the selected FMOD output/driver, logs and records its hardware-3D/EAX capabilities, applies buffer size and min-hardware-channel settings, calls FSOUND_Init, and configures the 3D rolloff, doppler, and listener attributes.
Tears down the sound device by walking the active sample and stream lists to stop and free each entry via vtable callbacks, then closes FMOD and clears the initialized flag.
Closes the FMOD stream owned by the given sound object, frees its stream record, and clears the object's stream pointer.
Returns true if the sound object's channel is valid and FSOUND_IsPlaying reports it is currently playing.
Returns true if the sound object's channel is invalid or FSOUND_IsPlaying reports it is not currently playing.
Copies the sound object's flag byte (offset 0x54) into the associated stream record (offset 0x18) when a stream is present.
Stores the given enable flag into the object (offset 0x24) and tail-calls the device vtable slot at 0x10 to apply the change.
Stores the requested record-enable flag into the object (offset 0x25) and starts FMOD recording only when both the enable (0x24) and record (0x25) flags are set, otherwise stops recording.
Returns the byte flag at offset 0x18 of the sound's sample/stream descriptor (pointer at this+0x48).
Returns the float field at offset 0x88 of the sound's sample/stream descriptor (pointer at this+0x48), or 0.0 if the descriptor is null.
Returns the sample/descriptor count stored at offset 0x44 of the sound object.
Bounds-checks the index against the sample count and, if valid, copies the indexed 0x98-byte sample descriptor from the sound's descriptor array (this+0x3c) into the output buffer.
Creates an FSOUND streamed or static sample for a sound instance, starts playback on a free channel, and applies its volume, frequency, and min/max 3D distance before marking the instance active.
Stops the FSOUND channel held at offset 0x40 of the sound instance, bumps the stop counter, sets the stopped flag, and resets the channel handle to -1.
If the sound instance owns a stream object (ptr at +8), flags it to stop; otherwise invokes the instance's stop and release virtual methods (vtable+0x5c then +0x58).
Maps the configured speaker-mode setting (DAT_006790d0) to the corresponding FSOUND speaker mode and applies it via FSOUND_SetSpeakerMode.
Returns a human-readable description string for the given FSOUND error code (passed in EAX), or "Unknown error" for unrecognized codes.
Copies up to the requested number of bytes from the source into the stream's circular buffer, wrapping around the end, advancing the write index, and returning the number of bytes actually written.
Copies up to the requested number of bytes out of a voice ring buffer, wrapping from the read offset past the end back to the start, and advances the read offset.
Zero-initializes all buffer pointers, offsets, codec handles, and counters of a voice stream object prior to allocation.
Allocates the PCM and packet buffers for a voice stream and, per the mode flags, sets up the encoder codec (bit 1) and/or decoder codec (bit 2) and the side scratch buffer.
Frees all buffers held by a voice stream and tears down its encoder and decoder codec objects according to the mode flags.

Feeds captured PCM samples into the encode frame buffer, and on each full frame computes the peak level, runs voice-activity detection, and either encodes/transmits the frame or discards it as silence.
Pulls length-prefixed encoded voice packets from the accumulator, decodes each one into PCM through the decoder codec, compacts any leftover bytes, and returns the decoded PCM buffer and size.

Fills the requested number of output bytes for playback by draining leftover ring-buffer data then decoded voice PCM, zero-padding any shortfall and discarding excess voice data beyond the buffer capacity.

Appends an encoded voice frame to the accumulator buffer (writing a 4-byte length prefix and running the encoder when called with a null payload), reporting and counting an overflow when the buffer is full.
Resets the encoder codec state of a voice stream when the encode mode flag is set, flushing it with an extra reset pass on the first invocation.
Initializes voice capture by selecting the FSOUND record driver and allocating a looping record sample, storing the sample handle and a status code in the result struct.
Stops FSOUND recording, resets the read cursor, and locks/unlocks the record sample to zero-fill its entire buffer, returning success when cleared.

Reads the current FSOUND record position and locks the newly captured sample region between the last and current cursor, feeding both wrapped halves into the voice encoder before unlocking and advancing the read cursor.
Zero-initializes the 16-byte stream-voice slot (playing flag, sample pointer, FSOUND stream handle, and channel id).
Destructor wrapper for a stream-voice slot that simply forwards to Voice_StreamStopAndClose.
Stops the stream-voice's FSOUND stream if playing (logging FSOUND errors on failure) and then closes the stream handle.
Starts the stream-voice playing via FSOUND_Stream_PlayEx, applies the computed volume and unpauses the channel, logging FSOUND errors and marking the voice active on success.
FSOUND stream callback that zeroes the requested output buffer and refills it from the stream-voice's playback voice ring buffer.

Allocates the playback voice array and stream-voice array, creates one FSOUND stream per voice using Voice_StreamReadCallback, and constructs the local RecordVoice, reporting an error if recording cannot be set up.
Tears down the voice system by destroying and freeing the stream-voice array, the playback voice, and the RecordVoice, stopping recording and freeing the FSOUND record sample.
Begins looping FSOUND capture into the RecordVoice's sample, logging the FSOUND error and storing error line 0x33a if recording fails to start.
Iterates over every active voice-sound entry in the list and calls FSOUND_SetVolume on each channel, logging an FMOD error from sound_voice.cpp if a call fails.
Drains the recorded mic sample, and once at least 160ms has elapsed since the last send, decodes the queued voice packets and transmits the resulting sample over the network.
Builds a rotation matrix from the entity's stored Euler angles and integrates its position and velocity forward by the elapsed-time delta to produce a dead-reckoned predicted transform.

Converts the entity's current and target Euler angles to quaternions and, if the angular gap exceeds the threshold, spherically interpolates between them and writes the smoothed orientation back as Euler angles, otherwise snaps to the target.

Computes the position-error vector between the entity's predicted point and the reference point, stores its length, normalizes the direction when the error exceeds the threshold, and snapshots the current orientation for blending.

Advances the entity's interpolated position toward the reference along the error vector by a time-scaled fraction and invokes the orientation extrapolation and slerp steps, flagging whether any correction is still pending.

Snaps the entity's interpolated position to the authoritative reference when within the distance threshold and likewise snaps its orientation when the quaternion angle is within the angular threshold, eliminating residual prediction error.
Sends a SQUAD_ANSWER_INVITE network message with the decline flag (0) carrying the inviter's id and squad id, then removes the matching pending-invite entry.
Sends a SQUAD_ANSWER_INVITE network message with the accept flag (1) carrying the inviter's id and squad id, then removes the matching pending-invite entry.
Iterates the pending squad-invite list, sending a SQUAD_ANSWER_INVITE decline message for each inviter/squad pair and removing every entry until the list is empty.
If no existing invite matches the inviter's player and squad id, allocates an {entry,id} node, appends it to the squad-invite list, and prints "%s has invited you to join %s!" to the console.
Removes every squad-invite node whose player id and squad id match the given pair, frees the node and its payload, and (unless suppressed) prints "%s is no longer asking you to join %s!".
Removes any existing squad-definition entry whose id matches the new record's id and frees it, then prepends the new entry to the squad-entry list.
Removes any existing squad-member record with the same id and frees it, prepends the new member record to the squad-member list, then refreshes the matching player's secondary name.
Scans the squad-entry list and returns the entry record whose id equals the local player's squad id, or null if none matches.
Finds the squad-entry record whose id equals the local player's squad id, unlinks it from the list, and frees the record and its payload.
Looks up the local player's entity record, reads its linked member id, and returns the squad-member record matching that id, or null if not found.
Iterates over a tiled/swizzled source bitmap region and, for each source pixel that differs from the surface's transparent color, writes the given fill byte into the destination buffer.
Clips a sprite's rectangle against the destination surface bounds and blits each visible row of the source bitmap via Rast_BlitGlyphRowsMasked using the given fill color.
Computes the byte offset into a surface for the given x/y, using the swizzle lookup tables for tiled (type-3) surfaces and a plain row-stride multiply otherwise.
Fills the given number of surface rows (or the full height when count is -1) with a single byte value by memsetting each row of the pixel buffer at the row stride.
Writes a single color byte to the surface at rounded float coordinates only if the point lies inside the surface clip rectangle (offsets 0x1c-0x28).
Clips a sprite against the destination surface bounds and copies it row by row with memcpy as an opaque (non-transparent) blit.
Clips a sprite against the destination surface and blits it row by row, translating each source pixel through a palette remap table from Palette_LookupEntry.
Looks up the texture's per-mip width and source pointer from the global mip tables and forwards them to Raster_BlitTexturedRect to draw the scaled texture tile.
Clipped sprite blit that uses a fast memcpy path when the alpha factor is 1.0 and a per-pixel palette-remap path otherwise, falling back to Raster_BlitTextureScaled when the mip level does not match.
Clips a sprite against the destination surface and blits it row by row as a transparent color-keyed copy, writing only source pixels that are non-zero.
Draws a single-color line between two endpoints directly into the surface pixel buffer using an integer Bresenham line algorithm.
Clips a line to the surface clip rectangle using the Cohen-Sutherland outcode algorithm and, if any part is visible, draws it via Raster_DrawLineUnclipped.
Draws a shaded/beveled rectangle by stroking its four edges with light and dark shades derived from a palette entry and plotting the two opposite corner pixels.
Copies a rectangular sprite region into the destination buffer row by row, skipping the transparent key color and remapping each remaining pixel through the given color-translation table.
Clips a sprite blit at (x,y) against the destination surface's clip rectangle, resolves the palette translation table, and dispatches each visible scanline to Sprite_BlitSpanRemap.
Iterates over the grid cells within the given bounds, computes a distance-based brightness falloff for each cell, and calls the surface's vtable plot method to shade the cell.

Queries the surface's bitmap dimensions and stride via vtable, allocates a tightly-packed buffer, and copies the pixels row by row (flipping when the stride is negative) returning the buffer and an 8-bpp tag.
Reads a little-endian 32-bit value from the stream cursor into the output, advances the cursor by 4 and decrements the remaining byte count, returning false if fewer than 4 bytes remain.
Reads a little-endian 16-bit value from the stream cursor into the output, advances the cursor by 2 and decrements the remaining byte count, returning false if fewer than 2 bytes remain.
Serializes every stripmap entry in the global list (counts, vertices, and pixel data) into a memory buffer and writes it out as the "stripmaps2" archive at c:\\ntank\\data.
Allocates a stripmap entry, duplicates its name, then parses the strip count, width, height, pixel data, and triple-short strip records out of the supplied byte buffer.
Opens the "stripmaps2" pack file, seeks and reads each catalogued blob, parses it with StripMap_ParseEntry, and inserts the resulting entry into the global stripmap list.
Walks the linked list of strip records, copying their triple-short headers into one contiguous array and their pixel spans into one concatenated buffer stored in the target struct.
Scans one bitmap pixel row for runs of non-zero pixels and allocates a 12-byte span record (start x, row index, run width, pixel pointer) for each run, appending it to the given span list.

Builds a named stripmap entry by duplicating the name, scanning every row of the source bitmap into a temporary span list, packing the spans into the entry, then freeing the temp list and appending the entry to the global stripmap list.

Looks up a texture by name in the texture hash table, computes its pixel base address (accounting for tiled-format stride when format==3), and builds a stripmap entry from that texture's pixels and dimensions.

Returns the stripmap for the given name: ensures stripmaps are loaded, searches the cached list by name, then falls back to building from a matching texture, and finally to loading "screen/NAME.BMP" from disk and registering it as a new texture and stripmap.

Iterates the global stripmap list and writes a formatted line (index, name, glyph-span count, summed glyph width) for each entry to the given console/output sink, or reports that stripmaps are not loaded yet.

Advances a span-packing cursor by the given amount, growing the current row height, and when the cursor reaches the row end it wraps to the next row, resets the position and height, and recomputes the remaining width.

Tests a span against the packing cursor's leading region and, if the overlap fraction and resulting fill ratio both pass their thresholds, consumes that portion by advancing the cursor and shrinking the remaining length, returning whether the span was fully handled.

Tests a span against the packing cursor's trailing region and, if the overlap fraction and resulting fill ratio both pass their thresholds, consumes that portion by extending the cursor length, returning whether the span was fully handled.

Compares one span's row against the cursor row and, on a match, computes the horizontal overlap with the cursor window via the start/end split helpers and adds that overlap width to the run's accumulated coverage count.

Walks the span list for one row, sums each span's horizontal overlap with the candidate run, and if the total coverage ratio meets the threshold it commits the overlapping spans into the run, increments its span count, and returns the next list node.
Walks the free-rectangle list merging adjacent nodes while the accumulated span stays within the 126-pixel strip width limit.
Allocates a new free-rectangle node (x, y, width, atlas-offset) plus its list wrapper and splices it into the doubly-linked free list, incrementing the node count.
Copies a source glyph run into the strip atlas advancing the destination by the row stride each step, producing a 90-degree rotated (column-wise) blit.
Copies a source glyph run byte-for-byte into a horizontal row of the strip atlas at the computed pixel offset.

Scans the free-rectangle list for a node overlapping the requested band, splits off the unused left/right remainders, unlinks the consumed node, and blits the glyph into the atlas either rotated or straight.

Clamps the next glyph to the current texture page's remaining width and height, builds a 12-byte placement record, runs the allocator/blit, and appends the record to the output list, returning true on success.
Builds the initial free-rectangle list from the source glyph table, allocating a 12-byte node per 6-byte glyph entry and assigning each a running horizontal atlas offset.
Packs all source glyphs into 128x128 stripmap texture pages allocated via TexCache, blitting each glyph and finally copying the collected placement records into the owner's array.
Formats a printf-style message into a dynamically grown heap buffer and appends a new node carrying the type, id, and text to the message list at param_1+0x40.
Walks the global message list and unlinks then frees every node (and its text buffer) whose id field matches the given id.
Converts an (x, y, width, height) rectangle into edge coordinates and forwards them to Table_SetGeometryAndLayout to position and lay out the table widget.
Stores the table widget's x/y/width/height and derived pixel rectangle and row-metric fields, then invokes the layout vtable callback and the row-region update to recompute the visible rows.

Tests whether a mouse-button input event falls inside the table's content rectangle, computes the clicked row index, and invokes the table's row-selection callback for that row, returning true if handled.
Renders the table widget by drawing its optional filled background, header label, bordering frame, scrollbar thumb position, and the text of each currently visible row via the render device vtable.
Walks the table's row linked list, unlinking each row node and freeing both its text payload buffer and the node itself.
Constructs a Table widget: installs its vftable, initializes its default state and row container, and allocates and configures the child scrollbar with its palette and clamped track window.

Constructs a Tank_Client: installs the Vehicle_Client then Tank_Client vftables, allocates and initializes its model/animation subobject, binds it to the entity type, and runs the initial engine-zoom reset.

Resets the vehicle client's zoom counter and reads the entity's base zoom value into its current/target fields, then updates the global engine-zoom level clamped to its min/max range and flags it changed.
Returns true when the vehicle is under engine load, i.e. its current zoom lags its target and any of its four motion-component magnitudes squared exceeds the threshold constant.

Per-frame update that counts sustained engine load and, once held for several frames, drives the engine-zoom slider to twice the entity speed and syncs the new zoom target to the synchronized channel.

Reads the double target value from the event's action object, writes it to control-channel slot 5, pushes it to the sync channel via Sync_SetChannelTarget, and caches it in the event's current/target float fields.
Sets the caller's "value present" output flag to 1 and returns the cached target float stored at offset 0x14 of the object.
Frees each node's payload buffer in the singly linked list, clears the list head/tail, and frees the list object itself (with SEH frame teardown).
Returns true only if the passed list matches the global list (DAT_006784d4) in header fields and every node's first payload word compares equal element-by-element.
If the global list (DAT_006784d4) exists, destroys its nodes, frees the list object, and nulls the global pointer.

Looks up the entity at the given index in the target array, stores it as the current/selected target globals, sends a RETARGET network message, and sets a flag when the entity is a type-0x14 object matching the active context.
Computes each draw-list entry's scalar key (storing it at +8), finds the min/max across the list, then scales each entry's alpha/weight by a normalized 1.0-((key-min)/range)*factor falloff.

For each draw-list entry, builds the normalized direction from the camera to the entity, dots it against the rotated view axis, and zeroes the entry's weight (and scales its alpha) when the dot is on the wrong side of the given threshold.
Computes the cosine threshold from the object's angle and forwards it to DrawList_ApplyViewConeCullWeights to cull the draw list against the view cone.
For each draw-list entry, reads the entity's damage value (clamping negatives to zero) and its type's max from the type table, then scales the entry's weight by 1.0 minus the damage ratio.
Scales each candidate's target score by its entity health/value (+0xd0) divided by the per-type weight from the type table, clamping negative results to zero.
qsort comparator that orders two candidate records by their score field (+4) in descending order.

Builds a temporary {entity,score} array from the candidate list, runs the registered scoring callbacks, sorts by descending score, drops the zero-score tail, and writes the surviving entity pointers and count back.

Scans the active input-command list to derive a target-cycle direction bitmask and stores its bits into the global cycle-direction flags, swapping next/previous according to the player's team/view side at entity+0xf0.
Returns true when the given candidate entity is on a different team than the player and is either a special override type or has been alive longer than the lock-eligibility delay.
Returns true only when both control command 5 and command 0x15 are present in the active input-command list.

Allocates and fills an array of all entities that pass the targeting filters (cycle-direction flag, active, not self, eligible, alive, and not a hidden lock type), ranks them, and returns the candidate pointer array and count.
Frees the previous global target-candidate array and rebuilds it, refreshing the global candidate pointer and count.
Returns the index of the currently locked target within the global candidate array, or -1 if it is not present.
Selects the next target in the global candidate array (wrapping to the first), or the first one if no target is currently locked.

Allocates a 0x20-byte target-spec entry, copies the spec name (NEAREST or FURTHEST variant per DAT_006784bf) from the spec table at index param_1*6, and initializes its index, name pointer/length, direction flag, and 0xfa-byte work buffer.

Installs the pending target-spec list as active: when disabled (DAT_00678108==0) it frees the current list, sends a retarget(-1) and resets selection state, otherwise it activates the new list and applies it via FUN_00491080.

Clears the active target list, builds a default target-spec list (specs 0, 6 and 0x10 with their enable flags), commits it, then selects the initial cycle target and re-selects the local team-slot entity.
Builds an alternate preset target-spec list (specs 0, 2 and 0x14 with their enable flags) and commits it as the active target list.
Frees the active target-spec list (DAT_006784d4), resets the target-cycle bookkeeping globals, and sends a retarget(-1) to clear the current network target.
Case-insensitively compares two strings character by character, returning true once the first string is consumed (i.e. it matched as a prefix of the second).
Searches the target-spec name table (stride 6 from PTR_s_NEAREST_00577690) for a case-insensitive prefix match, returning the matched spec index and an exact-match flag.

Parses a list of targeting-spec name arguments, looking each up and appending its spec entry with the right flags, reporting an "Unknown targeting spec" error on a bad name, then commits the list and updates the current cycle target and team-slot selection.
When an active target list exists and its flags at +0x14 mark it as one-shot/transient (and selection occurred), rebuilds the default target list.
Resets the 40-byte per-entity-type targetable flag table at DAT_005f60a8 by filling all ten dwords with 0x01010101 (every type enabled).
Dispatches on a menu-event code to set the corresponding per-item redraw/dirty flag bytes, resetting all of them for the reset codes 0x14/0x15.
Ticks the row's highlight-decay timer (marking it selected when it expires) and draws the row's two text strings via the renderer vtable at +0x9c.
Walks the active selection-menu's linked list of rows, drawing each via Select_DrawItemRow and advancing the vertical pixel offset by each row's height.
Closes the given selection menu, clearing the active/open menu globals, cancelling any retarget via Net_SendRetarget(-1), and tearing down the row list for certain menu types.
Resolves the texture handle for a selection row, falling back to the named player's texture (via Player_FindByName) and caching that handle on the row when the primary lookup fails.
Initializes a selection row from the current target, freeing any old label, storing the target id, and duplicating the matching player's name into the row when found in the player list.
Constructs a Team_Selection_Box, installing its vtable, allocating its three FloatTrack animators and a Scrollbar, and initializing its layout fields and clamped track window.
Replaces the box's label string with a duplicate of the source text, recording its length and copying the associated id and palette/color value onto the box.
Word-wraps the box's label into up to three lines that fit the box width and draws each line (with a shadow/background pass) via the renderer vtable.
Selects the open/close FloatTrack based on the box's current vs target category and advances it to produce the box's fade/expand fraction, clamped into [0,1].
Draws a team-selection box: fills its background rectangle and draws the team icon scaled by the box's fill fraction, then renders the team title text.
Inserts a player record into the scoreboard's doubly-linked list keeping it ordered by the player's score field at +0x28 (descending), allocating a 0xC-byte list node.
Builds the sorted player list for the selected team and renders the scoreboard rows (Rank/Tag/Kudos/Kills/Ratio) with a scrollbar, or "No players on this team." when empty.
Draws a team panel: counts the team's players, renders the centered "%d players"/"1 player" label over a fill bar, then draws the player scoreboard.
Handles a left-button click on a team box: if team switching is allowed and not at capacity, plays the UI select sound and sends a team-join/reincarnate selection to the server.
Populates the team-selection screen layout globals with the hard-coded screen positions, sizes, and draw callbacks for the two team boxes and their labels.
Builds the team-selection screen: constructs the two team-box widgets, registers the team-switch status/error message strings, and creates the info/list widget.
Looks up the status message by code, frees the previous markup document, and rebuilds the team-select info widget's rich-text document.
Once per session (guarded by a flag), sends the server a reincarnate/team selection picking the local player's team based on the current team comparison.
If the access-denied reason string is non-empty, pops up a "Server Access Denied" message dialog containing that text.

Looks up the tile IDs for the neutral and two team-colored bitmap names, logging a TEAM_TILEMAP warning for any missing tile, and appends the resulting {neutral, team1, team2} triplet to the team-tilemap remap list.

Searches the team-tilemap remap list for an entry containing the given tile ID and returns the tile ID for the requested team color (slot 1 or 2, otherwise neutral), or the original ID if no entry matches.

Iterates over every face of a shape, looks each face's tile ID up in the team-tilemap remap list, and writes back the team-colored tile ID (slot 1 or 2, otherwise neutral) into the shape's per-face tile array.
Populates the team-tilemap remap list by registering all known structure/vehicle texture names paired with their team-colored variants.
Initializes a packed terrain-vertex record, setting its two 9-bit index fields to 0x1ff and clearing the remaining fields.
Fills a 16-byte terrain edge/neighbor record with 0xffff sentinel values to mark it as empty.
qsort comparator that decodes the height of two packed terrain vertices (via the active patch node's height table and scale/bias) and returns -1/0/1 ordering them by decoded height.

Builds the patch node's 0x121-entry vertex index array (packing each vertex height into the high bits), sorts it by height with TerrainVtx_CompareByHeight, and resets the node's index iteration cursor and count.
Maps a single-bit mask (1,2,4,...,0x40) to its 0-based bit index 0..6, returning -1 for any other value.

Returns the absolute height error of a packed terrain vertex versus the midpoint of its two edge neighbors (zero if both neighbor indices are the empty 0x1ff sentinel), used to drive patch LOD detail.

Builds one terrain quadtree patch node: scans its 17x17 (0x121) vertex block for min/max height and brightness, packs height and lighting indices into each vertex word, and computes the node's bounding-box center, extents, and bounding-sphere radius.

Recursively rebuilds every node of the terrain quadtree, calling Terrain_BuildPatchNode on the current node and descending into its three child subtrees plus its sibling chain until a leaf (node+0x754==1) is reached.

Recursively rebuilds only the terrain quadtree nodes whose bounds (node+0x744/0x748/0x74c/0x750) overlap the given grid rectangle, calling Terrain_BuildPatchNode on each visited node and descending into its children and sibling chain.

Allocates a grid of terrain quadtree patch nodes (0x790 bytes each) sized to the heightmap divided by the given patch stride, constructs each node, fills in its grid extents/stride fields, and returns the node array while writing the column count to *param_3.
Links each parent node of one quadtree level to its four child nodes in the finer level below and writes the parent back-pointer (+0x768) into all four children.

Computes the (unnormalized) face normal of the first-orientation triangle of a terrain grid cell via the cross product of its two edge vectors, writing the xyz result through the in_EAX output pointer.

Computes the (unnormalized) face normal of the second-orientation triangle of a terrain grid cell via the cross product of its two edge vectors, writing the xyz result through the in_EAX output pointer.

Computes a terrain vertex's shading by averaging its surrounding triangle normals and dotting with the sun direction plus a Laplacian curvature/ambient-occlusion term, maps the result to a palette index, and packs that index into the vertex word.

Scans the heights over a rectangular block of terrain vertices to find their min and max, updates the active node's stored low/high bounds (node+0x1c/+0x28), and dispatches either a rect-limited or full quadtree rebuild depending on whether the bounds changed.

Allocates and builds the full terrain LOD quadtree from a heightmap, generating successively coarser node-grid levels (doubling the patch stride each pass) via Terrain_AllocLevelGrid and linking each finer level to its parent with Terrain_LinkChildNodes until a single root remains.

Clamps the two input coordinates into the 0..0x10 (17x17) grid, computing the linear index row*0x11+col, and returns either the plain index or, if either axis overflowed the grid edge, a negated value packing the wrap-direction quadrant bits (0x800/0x200) with the index.

Recursively subdivides the 17x17 terrain mesh, writing the subdivision level and four encoded neighbor/child edge indices into each node record (in the _DAT_005e6a00 and DAT_005e70c8 node arrays), setting child-present flag bits, and recursing into the four sub-triangles.
Decodes a mesh node's two packed edge codes back into grid row/column coordinates (div/mod 0x11) and writes the two reconstructed vertex indices into the caller-supplied short[2] output buffer.

Allocates and constructs the terrain LOD node arrays (DAT_005e70c8 and _DAT_005e6a00), builds the recursive subdivision tree and the two triangle binary trees, fills the per-node and coordinate-encoding lookup tables, and builds the renderer projection-step and sample lookup tables.

Recursively builds one triangle of the ROAM-style triangle binary tree by computing the min/max grid coordinates of its three corners, classifying its orientation, storing corners/midpoint into a freshly allocated 0x28-byte node record (array DAT_005f61a0, index counter DAT_006784ec), and recursing into its two child triangles; returns the node index.
Initializes a map tile-bucket object by zeroing its bucket-list head and the associated counter/state fields at offsets 0x734 through 0x78c.
Drains a map tile object's bucket list by repeatedly calling MapTileBucket_Recycle until the list head at offset 0x738 is empty.

Iterates the map's array of tile-row pointers (at offset 0x1c, count at 0x6c) and, for each non-null row, runs the array destructor (0x790-byte elements, destructor MapTileBucket_RecycleAll) and frees the backing allocation.
