Destroys a map object by releasing its four texture/resource handles at offsets 0xc-0x18 (resetting each to -1), freeing all tile-row arrays via Map_FreeTileRowArrays, and freeing the object itself.

Runs the client's main game loop: plays the startup sound, then forever measures the per-frame time delta (clamped to 500ms), services networking, interpolates entities, updates particle/HUD/FX systems, and polls and processes input each tick.
Frees and tears down the widget's child, string, and attribute lists then allocates fresh empty list containers for the latter two.
Sets the widget's byte flag at offset 0x28 to 1 (enabled/true).
Clears the widget's byte flag at offset 0x28 to 0 (disabled/false).
Stores the widget's left/top and computed right/bottom screen-rect edges then forwards x/y/width/height to the layout-update helper.
Walks the widget's child-widget list, unlinking each node, destroying the child via its cleanup helper, and freeing it.
Reads three string markup attributes and stores duplicated copies into the active widget struct fields 0x5c, 0x60, and 0x64, freeing any prior values.
Reads a markup attribute, allocates a one-pointer node holding a duplicated copy (or null), and appends it to the widget's string list at offset 0x38.
Constructs a Pad_Chunk widget, copying the layout's tex handle, setting default fields and vtable, then applying its initial bounds rect.
Initializes a Chunk widget, copying parent layout texture/flag/color fields, setting its vtable and default state, and linking it to its parent.
Replaces the chunk's stored text by duplicating the given string into a freshly allocated buffer, recording its length, and invoking the vtable layout callback sized by the per-character width.
Draws one text run/glyph: looks up its palette color, optionally selects its font texture, then issues the device draw call either scaled (with the given scale factor) or unscaled.
Virtual draw method for a text-run chunk that renders its run handle (this+0x30/0x34) at unit (1.0) scale via Markup_DrawGlyphRunScaled.
Virtual draw method for a text-run chunk that renders its run at the caller-supplied scale factor via Markup_DrawGlyphRunScaled.

Virtual event handler for a link/hot chunk: on a left-click (event type 1, code 5) it resolves the chunk's link index into the document's chunk array and stores the found target as the document's active link.
Resets the current layout line by computing the remaining line width (content width divided by the font space advance) and allocating a fresh empty word list for the line.

Finalizes the current word list into a laid-out line: measures each word's width/height, inserts left/right padding chunks for center/right alignment when needed, appends the line (with its max height) to the document line list, and resets line state.

Word-wraps the pending text against the line's remaining width by breaking at the last space that fits, appends each fitted word run to the current line, flushes the line when the width is exhausted, and repeats for the rest of the text.
Takes the accumulated text from the global working buffer, trims trailing spaces (unless inside a preformatted span), passes it to Markup_EmitWordsWithWrap for layout, and frees the buffer copy.

Main markup layout driver: walks the parsed markup node list and dispatches each tag opcode (font/color, alignment, link, embedded element, paragraph/line breaks, list indent) to build the laid-out line list for the document.

Hit-tests a point against the laid-out document: scrolls to the visible line for the given Y, walks each line's run chunks to find the one whose bounding box contains the point, and invokes that chunk's click/activate handler.
Walks the document's row list to sum total content height and find the widest row, then invokes the supplied callback with the computed maximum width and total height.
If the document is already built, measures each widget in every row and stores the tallest widget height as that row's height; otherwise rebuilds the widget lists from the markup first.
Sums the heights of all rows in the document's row list, writing zero to the optional width output and the accumulated total to the optional height output.

Computes the scrollbar position from total content height, clamps the track window, then draws each visible row's widgets left to right within the clip rectangle, advancing the x cursor by each widget's measured width.

Constructs a Document_Viewer object: installs its vftable, initializes scroll/layout fields and rectangle, allocates the Glowy chunk generator and the markup parser, and resets the widget lists to an empty document.
Destroys a Document_Viewer object: resets the widget lists, frees the parsed document and the row/column/widget list heads, destroys the embedded parser objects, and chains to the base destructor.
Installs the Chunk_Generator vftable into the object, constructing the base chunk-generator instance.
Allocates a new 0x44-byte chunk and, on success, builds it from the generator's source object, releasing the passed-in argument before returning the new chunk.
Lazily allocates a per-object stats node from the global free list, then increments its total count and the per-level bucket counter for the given level index.
Decrements the per-level bucket counter and total count on the object's stats node, releasing the node back to the global free list when the total reaches zero.

Walks the object's scheduled list, unlinking every node whose threshold is at or below the current counter, invoking each one's callback and returning its block back to the free pool while updating the pool's used count and lists.

Allocates the texture's pixel block from the texture cache, sets its width/height to 1<<level, initializes the mip-level count and edge/wrap bytes, and records the owner pointer plus the current cache generation.
Fills one mip level of a radial glow texture with 8-bit alpha values, computing each pixel from its distance to the center with a falloff curve and writing 0 outside the radius.
Allocates a new texture slot and its pixel block, clears it, then fills every mip level (0..param_1) with the procedural 8-bit alpha glow pattern and returns the new texture id.
Fills one mip level of a radial glow texture with 32-bit RGBA pixels, writing the same distance-based falloff intensity into all four channels of each texel.
Allocates a new texture slot and its pixel block in the 4-channel RGBA format, clears it, then fills every mip level (0..param_1) with the procedural glow pattern and returns the new texture id.

Pops the next free texture-slot id, pulls a texture object from the block pool (allocating a new block if empty), zeroes all of its fields, sets the default state/flags, stores it in the slot table and returns the object.
Allocates and initializes the global block allocator (40-byte items, 10 per block) used to hand out texture objects, storing it in the global pool pointer or null on out-of-memory.
Constructs a texture name-table entry by zeroing its first two bytes; used as the per-element constructor by the vector constructor iterator.
Looks up the given name in the texture name-to-id hash map and returns the stored id, or 0 if the name is absent or maps to the sentinel -1.
Loads a named tile via the global tile loader, and on failure logs "Unable to load tile '%s'!", shows a fatal reinstall dialog, and returns -1.
Grows the indexed texture-category's int array by one entry, copies the old contents, appends the given texture id, and updates the array pointer and count.
Rebuilds the indexed texture-category's int array omitting every entry equal to the given texture id, freeing the old array and updating the pointer and count.
Loads the named model file (falling back to a "_skinny" variant) into the current texture category, populates its texture list, and warns "can't find normal or skinny for <%s>" if neither loads.

Parses a "lock"/"unlock" command and a category name, then for the matching texture category either allocates and uploads each texture's chunk into the texture cache (lock) or decrements its reference counts and frees freelist blocks when they reach zero (unlock).
Initializes the texture cache: allocates the loader and the 5-entry texture-category array, zeroes the 32000-slot chunk table and id free-list, and builds the reserved placeholder chunk.
Builds the "bitmaps\\<categoryName>" path for the given texture category and loads that model/bitmap group into the cache.

Allocates a new texture chunk id, fills a chunk for the given indexed bitmap (uploading it into a cache block and building mipmaps when the dimensions match a power-of-two level, otherwise keeping a malloc'd copy), registers it, and returns the chunk id.
Allocates a new texture chunk and initializes its width, height, format/type, duplicated name string, and flag byte.

Seeks to the given file offset, reads a 3- or 9-byte texture header to determine format and dimensions, allocates a chunk, reads its pixel data from the file, registers it in the chunk table, and returns the chunk (or null on read failure).
Allocates a pointer array, loads every bitmap entry of the open pack via Tex_LoadBitmapFromFile, registers each loaded texture name in the global hash table, and returns the array and its count.
Writes a texture entry's header byte and dimensions to the output stream and appends its pixel rows, handling the format-3 cutout case (re-reading from disk when the mip level differs).

Builds the "c:\\ntank\\data\\bitmaps\\new\\<name>" path, serializes every texture of that pack slot into a memory stream while recording per-entry offsets, and writes the resulting bitmap pack file to disk.
Iterates over all bitmap pack descriptor slots and calls Tgen_BuildAndWriteBitmapPack for each named/eligible slot, returning false on the first failure or true when all slots are processed.

Releases a texture handle: invokes its destructor callback, unlinks it from the texture cache, frees its pixel memory, clears the slot in the handle table, and returns the texture id to the free-id stack.
Reserves an 8-byte-aligned chunk in the texture manager's scratch buffer, growing the buffer if the requested size exceeds the remaining room, and advances the buffer's used/free counters.

Returns the texture id of a cached "__cutout" sub-texture matching the source texture and rectangle, allocating a new power-of-two cutout entry and copying the sub-rectangle of pixels when no cached match exists.
Initializes the disk texture-generator module by installing the Tgen_Disk vtable and constructing its three bookkeeping list structures.
Tears down the disk texture-generator module by destroying its three bookkeeping list structures in reverse order.

Searches the texture cache's block lists for a slot matching the given block, replacing or merging an existing block (freeing it and adjusting free-space totals) or appending the new block, and unlinks the old cache region.

Services one pending texture LOD request by reusing a cached block, reading the block from file and inserting it into the active list while charging the memory budget, or requeuing it when the budget is exhausted.
Allocates a 0x18-byte texture-load request node, fills in its block handle, format, source descriptor and byte size, marks the source's pending-LOD field, and immediately tries to service it.

Per-frame texture-cache pump that completes finished async reads, uploads loaded texels into their block descriptors, frees the request nodes, then services queued load requests until the memory budget is reached and resets the budget.
Allocates a buffer sized for the block's LOD level, seeks to the block's file offset, reads its texel data via fread, and returns the buffer pointer and byte size.
Discards all pending and in-flight texture-load requests, restoring each affected block's current-LOD field, unlinking its cache block, and clearing both request lists.
Allocates and constructs the global texture-streaming/async-IO manager object and initializes the cache's per-frame memory budget.
Precomputes the 16 squared-radius escape thresholds and matching palette color indices used by the procedural escape-iteration texture generator.
Fills a size x size pixel tile by running a Mandelbrot-style escape iteration per texel and mapping the final squared magnitude to a palette index via the precomputed band tables.

Regenerates a texture block at the given LOD by unlinking the old cache block, allocating a new one, filling it with the procedural escape-iteration pattern, building its mip chain, and updating the block's LOD bookkeeping fields.
Computes a scaled palette color byte from a distance-based quadratic falloff, returning zero when the sample lies beyond the near threshold.

Computes a single-channel light intensity for each vertex of a terrain tile grid by summing distance-attenuated particle-light contributions onto the base ambient value, clamps to 0..0x7f0000, and stores them in the mono lightmap scratch table at DAT_0062f040.

Allocates a new texture-block descriptor, configures it as a "pre_lightmap" RGB565 texture sized for the tile's detail level, and registers it in the tile-handle table (DAT_00630280) returning the new block handle.

Computes per-vertex red/green/blue light intensities for a terrain tile grid by summing distance-attenuated particle-light contributions, applies gamma scaling, and stores the float RGB triplets in the color lightmap scratch table at DAT_0062f4d8.
Builds the colored RGB565 lightmap texels for a tile by computing per-vertex RGB intensities, clamping each channel, and packing the rounded values into the tile block's texel buffer.

Builds the grayscale RGB565 lightmap texels for a tile by computing per-vertex mono intensities, clamping, and packing the single value replicated across all three channels into the tile block's texel buffer.

Additively blends a bilinearly-interpolated light gradient (from the lightmap scratch table corners) onto one block of texel rows, advancing the interpolants by fixed-point steps scaled by the mip shift.

Composites the tile's source texture blocks into the lightmap texel buffer at the selected mip level, modulating each texel by the per-vertex light intensity (and at coarser mips upscaling via the gradient blend in Lightmap_AddInterpolatedGradientRow).

Composites the tile's source texture blocks into the lightmap texel buffer at the selected mip level by copying texels without per-vertex light modulation, calling the mip downsampler for coarser levels.

Selects the appropriate lightmap mip level from the camera-distance budget, unlinks any stale block, allocates texture-cache storage, and dispatches to the shaded or plain mip composer to (re)build the tile lightmap, returning whether it was built at full resolution.
Decrements the reference count of a lightmap block and, when it reaches zero, returns the block to the free pool (DAT_0067d8f0) and marks it as freed.

Raises an object's tile-grid texture detail to the requested mip level (clamped to 7), bumping per-tile mip reference counts and queuing load requests, then commits via Tex_CommitMipLevelChange; falls back to Tex_ReleaseToBaseMip when the level is zero.

Returns the existing tile-grid texture id when high-detail streaming is enabled and the node is ready, otherwise allocates a fresh texture entry, initializes its mip-level fields and flags, registers it in the texture-object table, and returns its id.
Invokes the object's stored completion callback (function pointer at +0x20 with argument at +0x24) if present, then re-runs Tex_SetObjectTileDetailLevel to reapply the texture detail level.

Frees the texture's high-detail cache block back to the texture cache, reloads it at the base mip level, resets its mip-level fields and flag bits, fills it with the object's solid base color, and notifies the renderer via the device vtable.
Walks the deferred texture-update list, restoring the active texture globals and calling Tex_CommitMipLevelChange for each queued node before freeing it, then publishes the new free-block watermark.

Initializes the texture subsystem by pointing four dispatch slots at a default handler, zeroing the 32000-entry texture-object pointer table, and installing the five per-state mip dispatch function pointers.

Rebuilds a texture's procedural mip palette, choosing the colored or the intensity-ramp generator based on a global mode flag, then copies the resulting max mip level into the current and base mip fields.
Empty no-op texture mip handler used as a default/placeholder dispatch slot.

Completes a queued texture mip-up load by allocating a larger cache block, copying the texel data into it, unlinking the old block, compositing any tagged overlay, downsampling, decrementing the pending-load counters, and firing the chained completion callback.

Requests raising a texture to the given mip level by allocating a load-request node and queuing per-child-tile load requests, installing a completion callback and bumping the pending counters, or completing immediately when nothing needs loading; downsamples in place when the requested level is below the current minimum.
Stub virtual method that always returns 0 (false).
Zeroes the entire 32000-entry global texture-tag-to-slot lookup table at DAT_0064f718.

Allocates a texture entry sized to the source surface, initializes its header fields, reserves space in the upload buffer, registers it in the tag-to-slot map, and composites and downsamples it into the tagged atlas.
Walks the active tagged-texture list decrementing per-slot reference counts and freeing slots whose count reaches zero, then frees the pending deferred-free buffer.
Builds a per-tag usage histogram across the given entity list and greedily promotes the most-referenced textures to their full mip level until the budget of 0x24 slots is exhausted.
Sets the Thermo widget's wrap-around flag (this+0x35) to 1, enabling value wrapping at the ends of its range.
Clears the Thermo widget's wrap-around flag (this+0x35) to 0, disabling value wrapping at the ends of its range.
Stops any currently playing UI tick voices and, if the sound source is active, plays the up or down tick sound effect selected by the boolean direction argument.
On a key-down event, steps the Thermo value down or up by one, clamping or wrapping it to the [0,max] range, plays the tick sound on change, and invokes the value-changed callback.
Constructs a Thermo bar widget: initializes its fields and vtable, sets its base widget rect, and resolves the menubar, bluebar, and barnotch texture ids by name from the UI image atlas.
Draws the Word_Thermo widget by blitting the background bitmap, the state-selected indicator bitmap centered and clamped within it, and the state-selected overlay bitmap aligned to that indicator.
Initializes a Word_Thermo widget instance, sets its vftable and default geometry, allocates its string pair block, and stores duplicated copies of the two given label strings.
Selects the Word_Thermo label string by its boolean state, measures its length, and renders it via the renderer text-draw call at the widget origin with brightness based on the highlight flag.
Initializes an Axis_Thermo widget, sizes it to 0x82x0x1b, and resolves the menubar, bluebar_lo/hi, and barnotch_lo/hi texture indices into its fields.
Draws the Axis_Thermo bar by blitting the bar background bitmap, the state-selected fill bitmap centered and clamped within it, and the state-selected notch bitmap aligned to that fill.
Handles mouse press/release events on the Axis_Thermo bar, capturing the cursor X coordinate on button-down and applying the dragged delta to the bound axis value on button-up.

Initializes an Integer_Thermo widget, stores its value and formatter callback, invokes the formatter to produce the initial display string, and stores a duplicated copy of it plus the formatted value.
Measures the Integer_Thermo display string and renders it via the renderer text-draw call at the widget origin, with brightness chosen by the widget highlight flag.
Handles step/scroll input on the Integer_Thermo (button 3 decrements, button 4 increments), re-runs the formatter callback, and replaces the stored display string and value.
Initializes an Input_Catcher widget, sizes it to match the owning panel's bounds, and registers it with the panel's child/input list.

Allocates a new MacsFrame, appends it to the view's frame list, then builds and cross-links its display Mode (cloned from the source frame, taken from a registered 'o' mode factory, or a default Empty_Mode), and returns the frame.

Constructs the editor's split-frame view manager: caches the global display, builds the root Input_Catcher/3macs Frame, initializes its frame and helper lists, creates the first frame, and registers the built-in 'Empty Mode' factory.
Tears down the view manager by calling the destroy virtual on every Mode in the frame list and every entry in the mode-registry list, then clears the active-frame flag.
Destroys and unlinks every MacsFrame in the view except the given keep-frame, then re-lays-out that surviving frame to fill the entire canvas (Emacs C-x 1).

Splits the current frame into a stacked top/bottom pair (Emacs C-x 2): shrinks this frame to the top half and creates a new frame bound to the same mode for the bottom half, if at least 0x40 rows are available.

Splits the current frame into a side-by-side left/right pair (Emacs C-x 3): shrinks this frame to the left half and creates a new frame for the right half if at least 0x80 columns are available, logging the new frame's bounds.
Default virtual stub used as a Frame/Mode vtable slot that always returns 0 (false).
Allocates a mode-registry entry holding a duplicated name string, a key character, and a constructor pointer, and appends it to the view manager's mode-factory list.
Searches the view manager's mode-registry list for an entry whose key character matches, optionally outputs its name string, and returns its constructor pointer (or 0 if none).
Frees every mode-registry entry's payload and its list nodes, then zeroes the manager's list head/tail/count and related fields.

Records a value at the given timestamp, either folding it into the existing exponentially-weighted running average or starting a fresh average and appending a new {value,timestamp} sample node to the list.
Walks the sample list and returns the sum of sample values divided by the age (in seconds) of the oldest sample within the given time window, or zero when none qualify.
Averages all sample values whose timestamps fall within the given time window, sets the caller's found-flag accordingly, and returns the mean (or zero if no samples qualify).
Iterates the sample linked list for a non-negative time window (an inlined-callback scan loop that walks each node), performing no other observable effect in this build.
Stamps the current frame time and pops/frees the oldest samples from the front of the list while they are older than the given max-age window.
Constructs a timed-sample averager object, initializing its sample list, storing the given window length, and clearing the accumulators.
Destructor for the timed-sample averager: frees every sample node in the list and releases the list's backing storage.
Brightens a loaded texture frame's palette indices by the global tint, downsamples it, then thresholds each pixel against the palette luminance to produce a binary (0/0xff) alpha/edge mask.

Allocates an animated-texture record for the named base, builds each "%03d"-suffixed frame name, looks up its texture index, promotes the bitmap to full detail, builds its alpha mask, and registers the record in the global texture list.
Formats a "%s%03d" frame name from a base string and frame number, looks it up in the global texture-name map, and returns its texture index or -1 if not found.

Looks up all textures matching the given base name, allocates a 0x30-byte alias-group node holding the primary texture id plus its numbered variants, and appends the node to the global alias list (printing an error if no texture matches).

Searches the global alias list for the group containing the given texture id (matching either the primary id or any variant), returning the group's primary id; if not found it lazily builds the group via TexAlias_LazyBuildFromName and retries once.
Finds the alias group whose primary id matches the input texture id and returns a randomly chosen texture from that group's variant list (rand() % (count+1), index 0 returning the primary id).
